articles.title: Could The Cowboys Miss The Postseason? Predicting Every NFC Division Winner
articles.summary: With the regular season quickly approaching, Colin Cowherd provided his division predictions and projected playoff field for the NFC on Wednesday's edition of The Herd.
articles.body: Will the Seattle Seahawks be able to fend off the Los Angeles Rams and win the NFC West again? Who will win the tight battle for the NFC North? With the regular season quickly approaching, Colin Cowherd provided his division predictions and projected playoff field for the NFC on Wednesday's edition of The Herd. Highlighting a mix of returning contenders and rising rosters, Cowherd forecasted three new playoff teams across the conference while breaking down all four divisions. "I've got three new playoff teams in the NFC: the Lions, the Saints, and the Giants," Cowherd said. Here's how Cowherd predicts the placement of all four divisions in the NFC. NFC East 1.Philadelphia Eagles Starting with the NFC East, Cowherd picked the Philadelphia Eagles to retain the division crown, pointing to roster continuity along the offensive line and past success under Jalen Hurts. "Jalen Hurts, since he became a full-time starter, has the winningest record in the NFL. I'm just going with this very, very well-run organization," Cowherd said. Despite losing A.J. Brown, Philadelphia added Dontayvion Wicks and drafted USC receiver Makai Lemon, returning all five offensive line starters with the seventh-easiest schedule in the league. 2.New York Giants Behind Philadelphia, Cowherd projected the New York Giants to finish ahead of the Dallas Cowboys for second place, should Jaxson Dart stay healthy. "They were one and seven last year in those one-score games, worst in the league," Cowherd said about the Giants. "And in fact, they blew five games in which they had a fourth-quarter lead. That is going to, even if it evens out, even if it doesn't totally flip, it will even out. If Jackson Dart can stay out of the blue tent, I think it's a playoff team." Following a tough year in close games in 2025, Cowherd thinks the scales will balance out for the Giants in 2026. 3.Dallas Cowboys Cowherd pointed to a trend from last season as the reason why he thinks the Cowboys could hold themselves back. "Here's the other thing, which has become a disturbing trend for the Cowboys. They were the most penalized team in the NFL last year. They did some big things well, like scoring. They did a lot of little things poorly. I have the Cowboys better, but not a playoff team." 4.Washington Commanders Washington was placed fourth in the division, pointing to roster turnover at key positions like left tackle and overall roster age as major obstacles for their prospects. "Washington just doesn't have enough talent. They lost Laremy Tunsil, their left tackle, who's a beast. Second-oldest roster in the NFL. I just don't like Washington right now going forward," Cowherd said. NFC North 1.Detroit Lions Moving to the NFC North, Cowherd went with the Detroit Lions to win the division, citing offensive firepower and draft adjustments. "I think the Lions have a combination of the best roster in the division and the easiest schedule in the entire league this year," Cowherd said. "I would argue quarterback, running back, tight end, wide receivers, they have the best group in the NFL." Cowherd added last year was considered a down year for Detroit and the offense still wound up amongst the league's best. "They were the only team to have a top-five scoring offense in the last four years. Even last year, when they struggled, it was top five." 2.Chicago Bears Last year's NFC North champions, the Chicago Bears, were picked to finish second in 2026 by Cowherd. "They were a great fourth quarter team last year. They probably can't quite equal that magic, but when they won the turnover battle, and nobody talks about this one, Chicago, they were 10-1 when they won the turnover battle," Cowherd said. Cowherd also pointed to Bears quarterback Caleb Williams, who does not have a history of turning the ball over. "Caleb Williams doesn't turn the ball over. He didn't in high school. He didn't in college. Even in the Eberflus year, 20 touchdowns, six picks. He is not a turnover quarterback. I have them for second." 3.Green Bay Packers The Green Bay Packers were picked by Cowherd to finish third in the division, despite the number of key pieces they have slated to return, ahead of the Minnesota Vikings. "Not only do they get Michael Parsons back in October, but they also get Tucker Kraft back, who looks to be a star young tight end in the NFL for years to come. Christian Watson got hurt. Jaden Reed got hurt," Cowherd said. Cowherd also suggested the Packers may have reached their ceiling. "They've not been a great September team, but they've been a wild card team in the last three seasons," Cowherd said. 4.Minnesota Vikings Minnesota landed in fourth place in Cowherd's prediction, but he said this shouldn't discredit what the Vikings are capable of. "Minnesota is going to be the best fourth-place team in the NFL," Cowherd said. "Christian Darrisaw is back at left tackle. I love the coach and the defensive coordinator. There's not a lot here I don't like, but Kyler Murray's backup is either J.J. McCarthy or Carson Wentz. I don't trust either." Despite an established coaching staff and offensive line talent, backup quarterback depth creates vulnerability behind starter Kyler Murray. Cowherd also pointed out how prone to turnovers and the injury history of all three quarterbacks on the roster. NFC South 1.New Orleans Saints The NFC South featured a surprise pick from Cowherd, with the New Orleans Saints taking first place behind quarterback Tyler Shough, thanks in part to a favorable schedule. "Second easiest schedule in football is the Saints," Cowherd said. "I thought they played very well at the end of last year. Tyler Shough, nobody paid attention, but they won four of their last five games." Cowherd added that the NFC South is usually unpredictable most seasons. "This is a division where you see teams go from last to first on a regular basis." 2.Carolina Panthers The Carolina Panthers were picked for second place, highlighting leadership under Dave Canales and general manager Dan Morgan alongside offensive line stability for Bryce Young. "I think Carolina has the coach and the general manager for the future. Dave Canales and Dan Morgan are excellent. I think they've given Bryce Young a lot to work with." Cowherd also pointed out the inconsistencies on the offensive line last year. "They had 11 different starting O-line combinations last year, so it was a bit of a mess in front of Bryce Young. I think they'll get that corrected," Cowherd said. 3.Tampa Bay Buccaneers Tampa Bay was picked to finish third by Cowherd, who pointed to recent offensive slumps, defensive regressions, and coaching pressure following late-season struggles. "You got a coach on the hot seat. You got a new offensive coordinator, 20th-ranked defense last year. No Mike Evans. Lost seven of the nine games down the stretch," Cowherd said. "So they were a bit of a mess offensively, and they weren't great defensively." 4.Atlanta Falcons Atlanta rounded out the division in fourth place, with Cowherd citing early road schedule challenges and unanswered questions at quarterback. "I like the coach, like the owner. I think the GM is pretty sharp. There's a couple of players like Drake London, a Bijan Robinson I love, but who's the quarterback? We don't know," Cowherd said. "Cross my fingers with Michael Penix, but they start with three of their first four games on the road." NFC West 1.Seattle Seahawks In the NFC West, Cowherd selected the Seattle Seahawks to claim the division title over the Los Angeles Rams, praising Seattle's performance in road games and young core talent. "Here's what I love about Seattle: the last two years best road team in the league, and I mean a fantastic road team, 15 and two," Cowherd said. "They're returning all their best players. All of them are in their prime." Cowherd went on to highlight the Seahawks' ability to win away from home and performance against other playoff teams as key factors. 2.Los Angeles Rams Cowherd placed the Rams second as Super Bowl contenders, acknowledging both Seattle and Los Angeles rank among the top teams in the league. "They return all 11 offensive starters. There's no reason to debate this. They could win the Super Bowl. I think these two teams, in my opinion, are the best two teams in the NFL: Seahawks, Rams, one and two in my book," Cowherd said. However, the hype surrounding the Rams is not enough to convince Cowherd. "I'll take Seattle to win over the Rams. Everybody in the world's telling me the Rams are going to win the Super Bowl. The team is hearing that. You know what?" Cowherd said. "They're going to be a really really good team and win 11 games. I think Seattle could win 12." 3.San Francisco 49ers San Francisco was picked to finish third by Cowherd, pointing to an aging roster coming off major surgical recoveries and defensive pass rush struggles. "They were 20th ranked in defense. They struggled to get to the quarterback. They have the oldest roster," Cowherd said. "They are highly reliant at left tackle, running back, edge rusher, linebacker on veteran players who are coming off injuries." 4.Arizona Cardinals Arizona was projected to finish fourth in the division as the team undergoes a rebuild while playing in arguably the toughest division in football. "Arizona, bit of a mess. 0-6 against the division last year," Cowherd said. "They're playing like the Jets for next year's draft. Arizona at fourth place." articles.title: Patrick Mahomes gets heartbreaking news as unexpected setback casts a shadow over his highly anticipated return
articles.summary: NFL News: Patrick Mahomes rarely finds himself outside the top tier of quarterback conversations. Yet as the 2026 NFL season approaches, ESPN has raised an unex.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes rarely finds himself outside the top tier of quarterback conversations. Yet as the 2026 NFL season approaches, ESPN has raised an unexpected question about his fantasy value. The issue is not a sudden loss of talent. It is what Mahomes may choose to do with his legs after a serious knee injury. That one change could have a major impact on how fantasy managers view the Kansas City Chiefs star.Patrick Mahomes’ fantasy ranking takes a surprising hitNFL insider Field Yates recently explained why a No. 15 fantasy ranking for Mahomes is not as shocking as it sounds.“To be very clear, nobody is saying Patrick Mahomes is anywhere close to the 15th-best quarterback in the NFL,” Yates said on ESPN. “I have him a little bit higher in my fantasy rankings, but that number 15 ranking overall is not that crazy of a thought, and there’s a very specific reason.”Fantasy football does not reward reputation. It rewards points, and Mahomes produced plenty of them on the ground last season.In 14 games during 2025, he threw for 3,587 yards with 22 touchdowns and 11 interceptions. He also rushed for 422 yards and five touchdowns, helping him average 22.7 fantasy points per game.Those rushing numbers mattered. The 422 yards were a career high, and his five rushing scores gave managers a valuable bonus that many traditional pocket passers cannot provide.That is exactly where Yates sees the biggest concern heading into 2026.“Greeny (Mike Greenberg), you may recall that last year Patrick Mahomes was running for his life. As a matter of fact, he scored the fourth most fantasy points per game of any quarterback last year just using his legs. He’s now coming off of a major knee injury. Patrick Mahomes will not be running nearly as much in 2026 as he did last season,” Yates added on Get Up, ESPN.Patrick Mahomes’ knee could change his Chiefs roleMahomes suffered torn ACL and LCL ligaments in his left knee during Kansas City’s Week 15 loss to the Los Angeles Chargers. His rehabilitation has progressed well, but the return of his natural mobility remains one of the biggest storylines surrounding the quarterback.The Chiefs have little reason to rush him. Their priority is having Mahomes healthy for the games that matter most.NFL insider Dan Graziano described seeing Mahomes test his movement during training camp, including throws while moving in both directions.“Mahomes seems ready for it. When I was there, Greeny (Mike Greenberg), he was testing the thing out, trying to see if he could move around, throw, you know, move around to his left and throw, move around to his right and throw, try and see if he has all the strength back in that. But so far, he has checked every box,” Graziano said.Kansas City has also added running back Kenneth Walker III, giving the offense another option to carry the rushing burden.For Mahomes, the challenge is different. He must regain confidence in his knee without feeling forced to prove anything with his legs. If he runs less, his arm will need to make up the difference.That could make his 2026 fantasy ranking more unpredictable, but it does not make him any less important to the Chiefs’ championship hopes.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Travis Kelce faces fresh NFL warning after $14,491 fine as league makes taunting and sportsmanship a major focus for 2026
articles.summary: NFL News: Travis Kelce has never been the kind of player to hide his emotions. The Kansas City Chiefs tight end thrives on intensity, big plays and fiery celebr.
articles.body: Travis Kelce has never been the kind of player to hide his emotions. The Kansas City Chiefs tight end thrives on intensity, big plays and fiery celebrations, but the NFL has reminded him that there is a line he cannot cross. With the league preparing to keep a close watch on taunting and unsportsmanlike behavior in 2026, Kelce may have to rethink how he channels that competitive edge.Travis Kelce and the NFL's stricter taunting rulesThe warning comes months after Kelce discovered that even a moment of emotion can have consequences. During Kansas City's September 2025 matchup with the Philadelphia Eagles, the veteran tight end made an obscene gesture toward the Philadelphia sideline after gaining 23 yards.The officials did not penalize him during the game. The NFL, however, reviewed the incident afterward and fined Kelce $14,491.That episode now carries extra weight because the league does not appear ready to ease its stance. Front Office Sports reported on August 26 that sportsmanship-related rules will remain a major point of emphasis for officials throughout the 2026 season.The focus includes taunting, illegal celebrations and fighting.“The NFL will continue its strict enforcement of taunting rules.Sportsmanship-related rules, including taunting, illegal celebrations, and fighting, will remain a point of emphasis for officials this season, sources tell FOS.”For Kelce, that means his trademark passion comes with a little more risk. His personality is part of what has made him such a compelling figure in the NFL, both on the field and beyond it. He plays with visible emotion, and that energy often spills into his celebrations.Travis Kelce faces a balancing act in 2026The issue is not whether Kelce can show emotion. Players are still allowed to celebrate and enjoy major moments. The challenge is knowing when a celebration becomes something officials view as directed at an opponent or as crossing the boundaries of sportsmanship.That distinction could matter for Kelce this season.His 2025 fine serves as a clear reminder that the NFL can review incidents after the final whistle and impose discipline even when no flag is thrown during the play. A gesture that feels harmless in the heat of competition can look very different under league review.Kelce does not need to change the competitive fire that has helped define his career. He simply needs to manage it.For the Chiefs star, the 2026 season could therefore become a test of control as much as performance. Every touchdown, first down and emotional exchange will carry the possibility of scrutiny.Kelce's decision is straightforward but important: keep playing with the same passion, while knowing exactly where the NFL's line is drawn. This time, crossing it could cost more than just a fine.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: “I realized that I was enjoying that so much more”: How Brittany Mahomes’ unexpected Iceland journey transformed her soccer dream into a career beyond the pitch
articles.summary: NFL News: Patrick Mahomes wife Brittany Mahomes travelled to Iceland in 2017 expecting to take the next step in her soccer career. She had just finished a recor.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes wife Brittany Mahomes travelled to Iceland in 2017 expecting to take the next step in her soccer career. She had just finished a record-setting college run at the University of Texas at Tyler and earned her first professional opportunity. But away from the pitch, Brittany found herself drawn to the gym and began creating workouts. That unexpected interest slowly changed the direction of her career and gave her a new path beyond soccer.Nearly nine years later, that decision has taken Brittany from professional soccer to fitness, business and ownership in women's sports. In 2026, she also reached a full-circle moment with her UT Tyler Hall of Fame induction, while raising three children with Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes.Brittany Mahomes went to Iceland for soccer but discovered a new passion away from the pitchBrittany Mahomes move to Iceland came after an impressive college career. Between 2013 and 2016, she made 74 appearances for UT Tyler, scored 31 goals and recorded 16 assists. Her 2016 senior season produced 18 goals and 40 points, setting single-season program records at the time. She also graduated with a kinesiology degree, which later helped her move naturally into fitness.On May 15, 2017, UT Tyler announced that Brittany had signed with Icelandic club UMF Afturelding/Fram. She played five matches during her only professional season and scored twice. The club won its league and earned promotion, but Brittany's time as a professional player ended after that campaign.Iceland, however, gave her more than professional playing experience. With fewer things to occupy her outside soccer, Brittany started spending more time in the gym, creating workouts and sharing them online. In her Feb. 2024 Sports Illustrated Swimsuit interview, she explained how that routine changed her thinking.“I didn’t have a ton to do outside of soccer, so I found myself spending a ton of time in the gym working out, creating workouts, and posting them online. I realized that I was enjoying that so much more than actually playing soccer,” Brittany said during the interview.That realisation gave her a reason to explore something beyond playing. Instead of forcing herself to stay on a path that no longer felt right, Brittany followed the interest she had discovered overseas. Her Iceland experience eventually brought Brittany Mahomes back to soccer in a different roleBrittany turned that interest into Brittany Lynne Fitness in 2019. She built an online training business around the fitness habits she had developed as an athlete. Her connection to soccer, meanwhile, never completely disappeared. On Dec. 7, 2020, she became part of the ownership group awarded an NWSL expansion franchise in Kansas City. The club became the Kansas City Current in 2021.The Current later opened CPKC Stadium in March 2024, giving the club a purpose-built home for women's professional soccer. Brittany had gone from trying to earn a place on the field to helping create a better platform for players.Motherhood has also changed what she wants from that work. Brittany and Patrick Mahomes now have three children, Sterling, Bronze and Golden. In an interview with Yahoo Entertainment, Brittany explained that she does not want to be defined by just one role.“I’ve never really wanted to define myself as one role. I feel like women are beyond capable of doing so many things at once,” she said.That outlook fits the journey that started in Iceland. Brittany went overseas as a young soccer player looking for her next opportunity. She returned with a new interest that eventually became a business and later helped lead her back into soccer ownership.In 2026, UT Tyler also inducted her into its Athletics Hall of Fame, bringing recognition to the college career that started the journey. For Brittany Mahomes, the road from Texas to Iceland and eventually back into women's soccer has not followed a straight line. The unexpected turn became the part that shaped everything that came after.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: NFL warns clubs they cannot sign any player who returns to college football for 2026 season, memo says
articles.summary: The NFL warned clubs that cut players returning to college cannot sign with a team this season, impacting LSU targets from the Browns and Saints.
articles.body: As the college landscape continues through a whirlwind of uncertainty, the NFL reiterated to its clubs on Wednesday that any player returning to college ranks will be prohibited from signing with a team this season. Multiple players in various sports are trying to return to college athletics despite going professional, which has led to quite the stir for the NCAA. Among them is tight end Dae’Quan Wright, who cleared waivers after being released by the Cleveland Browns this week. Wright was expected to sign with LSU, where he would reunite with his old Ole Miss coach, Lane Kiffin. CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM The league issued a memo, obtained by ESPN, that reiterated rules already in place saying any player signed to an NFL contract who is subsequently cut will be a free agent. While that player can sign with another NFL club or join the CFL, if they return to college, they will not be available for this season. Furthermore, any player cut by an NFL team who returns to college for the 2026 season will still be considered a free agent and won’t be able to put their name into a future NFL Draft. RAMS' SEAN MCVAY REACTS TO WILD COLLEGE FOOTBALL CONTROVERSY: 'FEEL LIKE I TOOK A FREAKIN' GUMMY' Other than Wright, Zxavian Harris, who was cut by the New Orleans Saints, is also expected to sign with Kiffin at LSU. He and Wright were teammates during Ole Miss’ College Football Playoff run last season, where Kiffin ultimately took the LSU vacancy mid-season after the firing of Brian Kelly. Both Wright and Harris received a temporary restraining order that allows them to return to college football, granting them an extra year of eligibility. But hours after Wright cleared waivers, he and the rest of the college football world saw the SEC and Big Ten, which will soon be joined by the ACC and Big 12, create new guidelines for eligibility that would prevent players like Wright who have participated in professional sports from reentering college athletics. Under the new policies set by the SEC and Big Ten, any athlete that has signed with a pro team in the NFL, declared for the NFL Draft or participated in any type of professional training camp will be ineligible for conference competition. Attorney Ryan Downton, who represents a number of players trying to get back into the college landscape, told OutKick’s Trey Wallace on Tuesday night that they are currently "working on a legal strategy" on how to move forward against both the NCAA and the respective conferences that enacted the new guidelines. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "The SEC’s actions put the NCAA in contempt of multiple court orders," Downton told OutKick-Fox News on Tuesday night. "It is cartel-like conduct when NCAA conferences attempt to create their own spur of the moment rules in response to Courts enjoining those same rules at the NCAA level."

articles.title: Why does Deshaun Watson continue to face Browns fans’ backlash? Here’s what NFL radio host Jim Rome had to say
articles.summary: NFL News: Deshaun Watson has the Cleveland Browns’ starting job, but winning back the fans could be much harder. Browns supporters booed him during the preseaso.
articles.body: Deshaun Watson has the Cleveland Browns’ starting job, but winning back the fans could be much harder. Browns supporters booed him during the preseason loss to the Buffalo Bills on August 22, and Watson later said the reaction felt personal. NFL radio host Jim Rome sees it differently. He believes the anger comes from Watson’s performance, his Cleveland tenure and the quarterback’s response to the criticism.The Browns still named Watson their Week 1 starter over Shedeur Sanders on August 24. That decision came after Watson completed just 5 of 12 passes for 36 yards against Buffalo. Sanders went 9 of 11 for 74 yards and a touchdown. For Rome, though, the issue stretches far beyond one preseason game.Jim Rome says Browns fans have reasons to turn on Deshaun WatsonSpeaking on The Jim Rome Show, Rome pushed back hard against Watson’s comments about the crowd. He argued that Watson cannot expect sympathy after failing to produce for Cleveland.“You go out, you play like a**,” Rome said on his show while discussing Watson’s performance against Buffalo. “And then you attack your own fan base again.”Rome then questioned Watson’s response to the boos, saying it showed “no accountability” and that the quarterback continued to blame others rather than accept responsibility.The radio host also made his central point clear. He believes Browns fans dislike Watson for both personal and football reasons.“Well, Browns fans are making it pretty clear that they don’t owe the creep a damn thing,” Rome said. “And they don’t, except booing him the next time they see him.”Rome’s criticism did not stop there. He argued that Watson has not given Cleveland enough on the field to expect unconditional support.“It’s both personal and performance-related for Browns fans,” Rome said.That view comes after a difficult Cleveland tenure. The Browns traded three first-round picks to the Houston Texans for Watson in 2022 and gave him a fully guaranteed five-year, $230 million contract. Since then, Watson has played only 19 games for Cleveland.Deshaun Watson’s Cleveland production has made the backlash harder to escapeDeshaun Watson arrived with a strong résumé. In 2020, his final full season with Houston, he threw for 4,823 yards and 33 touchdowns in 16 games.His Browns career has never reached that level. Injuries and suspensions have limited his availability, while his performances have left Cleveland searching for consistency.Rome revealed that frustration even more bluntly.“It seems to me they do hate the guy personally,” Rome added. “But they also hate the guy on the field too because all they’ve ever seen on the field since he arrived there is a** and garbage. And all they’ve ever seen off the field is a terrible, entitled, out-of-touch attitude. And again, with no remorse or contrition.”Now Watson gets another opportunity to change that perception. Cleveland will open the regular season against the Jacksonville Jaguars on September 13.The Browns have given him the job. The next step belongs to Watson. If his play improves, the noise could fade. If it does not, the boos may only get louder.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: What made Za’Darius Smith retire midseason? The heartbreaking family reason behind his decision
articles.summary: NFL News: Za’Darius Smith did not plan to retire from the NFL in 2025. He had just joined the Philadelphia Eagles and still had plenty left in the tank. But fiv.
articles.body: Za’Darius Smith did not plan to retire from the NFL in 2025. He had just joined the Philadelphia Eagles and still had plenty left in the tank. But five games into the season, one phone call changed everything. His mother’s doctor told him she did not have much time left. Smith then made a choice that put family ahead of football.The three-time Pro Bowler later faced more devastating losses. His mother died, followed by his grandmother and father within months. Now back with the Atlanta Falcons, Smith has opened up about the grief that pushed him into a dark place and the game that helped him find his footing again. A phone call changed Za’Darius Smith’s NFL plansSmith signed a one-year, $9 million contract with the Eagles in March 2025. He played five games before announcing his retirement in October 2025. He finished that short stint with 10 tackles, 1.5 sacks, two tackles for loss and three quarterback hits.The decision caught Philadelphia off guard. Smith had not planned to leave football. His family situation forced him to rethink everything.Speaking to reporters in Atlanta on August 26, 2026, Smith explained what happened.“I got a phone call from my mom’s doctor telling me that she don’t have much longer to be on this Earth,” Smith said during his Falcons press conference. “I let the team know. Obviously they wasn’t trying to let me leave. But that was the only thing I had left to retire.”Smith chose to spend that time with his mother. She later died, and the heartbreak continued. Smith also lost his grandmother and father within the following months.That stretch left the veteran pass rusher struggling away from football. Then, an unexpected call from Cleveland Browns general manager Andrew Berry gave him something to think about. Berry checked on Smith and eventually invited him for a workout. The workout went well, but the two sides could not agree on the money. Why Za’Darius Smith found his way back with the FalconsAtlanta eventually gave Smith another chance. The Falcons signed him to a one-year contract on August 18, 2026, reportedly worth $6 million with incentives that could push it to $8 million.The move also carried a personal connection. Smith reunited with Kevin Stefanski, his former Browns coach. More importantly, Atlanta had a special meaning for his late mother.“My mom always wanted me to be in Atlanta with the Falcons,” Smith said, according to his August 26 press conference. Atlanta also keeps him closer to his Alabama roots.For Smith, football now means more than sacks and statistics. It gives him a place to breathe again.“This is my happy place,” Smith said during the August 26 press conference. “I was in a dark place.”Smith enters his return with 70.5 career sacks and three Pro Bowl selections. After everything he has endured, his next target is simple: 100 sacks.The Falcons may have signed him for his pass-rushing ability. For Smith, though, this comeback carries something far more personal.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: What Tom Brady's leather pants confession tells us about the loneliest chapter of his life after the NFL
articles.summary: NFL News: Tom Brady has been retired from football for over two years now, but life outside the game is proving messier than most people expected from a man who.
articles.body: Tom Brady has been retired from football for over two years now, but life outside the game is proving messier than most people expected from a man who made precision look effortless. Since his 2022 divorce from Gisele Bündchen, Brady has been quietly piecing together a post-NFL identity -- one that now apparently includes leather pants, a Gucci runway, and another season calling games for Fox Sports. None of it looks quite the way anyone imagined. And that, oddly enough, makes it more interesting.Is Tom Brady dating anyone after his divorce from Gisele Bündchen?Tom Brady has stayed conspicuously quiet about his romantic life. No confirmed relationship, no public partner, no serious commitment that has held up to scrutiny. What exists instead is a string of high-profile links that kept gossip columns busy without ever really going anywhere.Irina Shayk was first. The two were spotted at events together through mid-2023, but whatever that was quietly evaporated. Brooks Nader's name surfaced in the summer of 2024. Then came the yacht sighting with Sofia Vergara in July 2025, which generated considerable online noise but no follow-up. Most recently, Brady was photographed looking comfortable with influencer Alix Earle during New Year's Eve celebrations in St. Barths.None of these have developed into anything Brady has acknowledged. At 47, navigating single life in the public eye is clearly a different kind of pressure than anything fourth-quarter football ever threw at him. The scoreboard there, at least, was always clear.Why is Tom Brady wearing leather pants and modeling for Gucci at 49?Here is where things get genuinely strange -- and genuinely human. Brady walked a Times Square runway for Gucci in May as part of a fall collection campaign. Leather pants. Full look. The image of a seven-time Super Bowl champion doing that registered somewhere between surreal and oddly admirable.His GQ interview afterward was the part worth paying attention to. Brady admitted he had never done leather before and seemed genuinely caught off guard by how much he liked it."Yeah, I'd never really done leather on leather before, but there are some leather pants in my closet now. I thought, Damn, that's actually really comfortable. I could see why people wear this," he said.He went further, drawing a comparison that only an athlete would think to make: "It's definitely a different look. It felt more like a uniform -- there was a rigidity and a structure to it, like my football uniform."That quote says more than it probably intended to. Brady spent 23 years in a uniform. Structure, rigidity, routine — those were the constants. Without them, he is clearly reaching for new frameworks to hang his identity on. Fashion is one. Broadcasting is another.On the Fox Sports front, Brady is heading into his third season as lead color analyst alongside Kevin Burkhardt. His first year drew mixed reviews — transitioning from elite player to credible broadcaster is harder than it looks. The second year was noticeably better. Fox has locked the pairing in for 2026, which suggests the network sees enough of a trajectory to stay the course.Put all of it together and what emerges is a portrait of someone still figuring out who he is when football is not the answer to that question. The leather pants are less a midlife crisis and more a man who genuinely does not know yet what comes next. That is not embarrassing. It is just honest.Tom Brady’s Palo Alto trading card store burglarized days after grand openingTom Brady’s newly opened trading card store in Palo Alto was burglarized less than two weeks after its grand opening, authorities said.According to the Palo Alto Police Department, suspects smashed a window and damaged multiple display cases at the CardVault location on El Camino Real late Saturday night. Around 60 trading cards worth more than $12,000 were reportedly stolen, ABC7 reported.The store officially opened on Aug. 15, with Brady attending the grand opening. articles.title: How Patrick Mahomes stays emotionally connected to Brittany even when the NFL locks him away at camp
articles.summary: NFL News: Patrick Mahomes is five weeks into his comeback from an ACL tear and logging seven hours a day of rehab at the Chiefs training camp in St. Joseph, Mis.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes is five weeks into his comeback from an ACL tear and logging seven hours a day of rehab at the Chiefs training camp in St. Joseph, Missouri. But when reporters caught up with him at a press conference on August 25, the conversation drifted away from football -- toward something Mahomes clearly thinks about just as carefully. He said he makes a point of texting wife Brittany even when the cell service at Missouri Western State University barely cooperates. For a man rebuilding one of the most scrutinized knees in sports, staying connected to home is not an afterthought.How does Patrick Mahomes keep in touch with Brittany during training camp?The dorms at Missouri Western are not exactly built for modern communication. Mahomes acknowledged as much with a laugh during his press conference, joking, "St. Joe's dorm rooms, man, you don't get a lot of text messages." But in the same breath, he made clear that one contact always gets through. "I just try to make sure I text Brittany," he said. "If I text Brittany, I'm usually in a good spot."That line is easy to brush past, but it says something real. Mahomes did not frame texting his wife as a sweet habit or a romantic gesture. He framed it as a personal barometer. When that line of contact is maintained, everything else feels manageable. For someone grinding through post-surgery rehab at the crack of dawn and then running full practice sessions, that kind of mental anchor matters more than most people realize.Head coach Andy Reid offered some context around just how consumed Mahomes has been with his recovery. Speaking to CBS Sports at camp, Reid described a quarterback who barely stops. "He just goes," Reid said. "He kept playing, he gets his rehab taken care of before and after practice, you know how he is." That schedule leaves little margin for anything else. So the fact that Mahomes actively carves out space to check in with Brittany -- even with spotty signal -- reflects a deliberate choice, not a passive one.Has fatherhood changed how Patrick Mahomes approaches training camp?Mahomes and Brittany have three children: daughter Sterling Skye, 5, son Patrick "Bronze" III, 3, and daughter Golden Raye, 20 months. Three kids under six years old is a logistical reality that any parent knows reshapes your sense of time and priority completely. Mahomes spoke to that shift earlier in camp on August 8, telling reporters that he has learned "to enjoy the little moments and enjoy the time at camp."That is not the language of a young quarterback chasing milestones. It is the language of someone who now understands what is waiting at home and wants to hold on to both worlds at once. Training camp used to be where NFL players disappeared into football. For Mahomes, entering his 10th NFL season, it has become something he has to navigate more intentionally -- balancing the demands of a historic comeback with the pull of a family that grew quickly while he was busy winning Super Bowls.Brittany and the kids have been close throughout his recovery from the ACL injury that ended his previous season early. That support has clearly filtered into how Mahomes talks about staying mentally grounded. A text message might seem like a small thing when you are staring down a $504.75 million contract -- the largest in NFL history, signed in June -- and a knee that needs to hold up for another decade. But Mahomes is telling you plainly what keeps the bigger picture in focus. Not the contract. Not the rings. Just knowing Brittany got the message.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Vinod Khosla: Seahawks' task is simple, keep winning and get another Super Bowl
articles.summary: Vinod Khosla, who was approved on Wednesday as the next owner of the Seattle Seahawks, says his expectation for the defending champions is more of the same.
articles.body:
Vinod Khosla, who was approved on Wednesday as the next owner of the Seattle Seahawks , says his expectation for the defending champions is more of the same.

"How often do you get to buy a franchise that has just won the Super Bowl, so we are incredibly lucky," Khosla said. "The task ahead is actually pretty simple: Keep the winning streak alive, get another Super Bowl. That simple."

Khosla said he and his family aren't just investing in football as a business, but as a passion.

"We are huge fans of football, and these opportunities, especially Super Bowl-winning teams, seldom come along, so we were very excited to have the opportunity," Khosla said. "We've been passionate about football for a long time."

Khosla has been a minority owner of the 49ers , so he understands the business of the NFL, and he said he has been a Steelers fan since emigrating to the United States from India in 1976, choosing the Steelers because they were the best team in the NFL at the time.

"I still watch all the Steelers' games," Khosla said.

Now, Khosla joins the famous Seahawks fan base.

"I think it's the best fan base in the country, of any NFL team. The 12s are such an iconic brand that it's hard not to be honored and humbled by inheriting that and being part of that fan base," Khosla said.

Asked about the future of Lumen Field and whether the Seahawks would renovate or build a new stadium, Khosla said it's too early to discuss that, as he hasn't even closed his deal to buy the team, but he sounded more interested in renovating the existing stadium than replacing it.

"Lumen Field is iconic and very much a part of the Seahawks brand," Khosla said. "We will work with management and with others and the community in Seattle, to hopefully preserve this iconic brand."

articles.title: ‘This Entire Charade Was Always About Trinidad Chambliss’ — CFB World Rips Louisiana Governor For Siding With LSU’s Lane Kiffin
articles.summary: Lane Kiffin continues to find himself at the center of attention, and his push to open the door for NFL returnees has become one of the latest major talking...
articles.body:
Lane Kiffin continues to find himself at the center of attention, and his push to open the door for NFL returnees has become one of the latest major talking points in college football.

In the middle of all the noise, Louisiana Governor Jeff Landry has made it clear he's firmly supporting the LSU head coach, prompting plenty of discussion across the college football community.

Lane Kiffin Gets Louisiana Governor's Backing in SEC Eligibility Battle

The latest eligibility dispute emerged after Kiffin pushed for the return of Zxavian Harris and Dae'Quan Wright to college football.

Kiffin and LSU are refusing to back down in their ongoing dispute with the SEC over the eligibility of former professional athletes. As the legal fight heads back to a courtroom in Baton Rouge, Landry has publicly thrown his support behind LSU's position.

Front Office Sports' Amanda Christovich reached out to Landry's office for his thoughts on the developing dispute between LSU and the SEC. The governor did not hold back, describing the situation as "ridiculous."

"Don't hate the player, hate the game," Landry said. "I've been saying for a year that college sports need to be fixed. The NCAA could have done it. Congress could have done it. Neither did."

Landry argued that the SEC has helped create the current legal situation by initially telling athletes that they had exhausted their eligibility, only for the rules to change later. He also pointed to the league's handling of previous cases involving Diego Pavia and Trinidad Chambliss, questioning why the latest situation should be treated differently.

However, Landry's comment didn't sit well with many in the college football community.

PREDICT THE CFB SEASON: PFN's Free CFB Playoff Predictor

"This entire charade was always about Trinidad Chambliss," one fan said.

"First time a sitting governor has ever said 'Don't hate the player, hate the game' in an on-the-record interview? Yes? No?" On3's Andy Staples asked .

"Lane and this dude are a match made in heaven," Yahoo Sports' Dan Wolken remarked .

The controversy gained further traction after CBS Sports reported that Kiffin and LSU had contacted multiple players currently on NFL rosters, or their representatives, to encourage them to pursue legal action against the NCAA and return to college football. That report adds some context to Kiffin's earlier justification that players are either going to play for LSU or play for another program.

However, Landry is willing to stand behind the LSU coach despite the growing criticism.

In defending LSU's position, Landry added that governing bodies cannot tell athletes that their college careers are finished, watch those players move on, change the eligibility rules afterward, and then penalize them for failing to anticipate those changes.

Meanwhile, critics continued to mock the governor's comments.

"Can't figure out if this is a Lane Kiffin tweet draft or a statement from a politician. Reads like the former. Wild that it's the latter," one said .

"Imagine Tate Reeves doing stuff like this," SportsTalk Mississippi's co-host Michael Borkey wrote .

"Some time down the road we are going to get a 30 for 30 type of show on LSU, and this guy won't be talked about kindly in it," Irish Breakdown's Bryan Driskell wrote .

Regardless of how the legal dispute ultimately unfolds, the situation proves just how aggressive Kiffin is willing to be in pursuing to improve LSU's roster.

After leaving Ole Miss shortly before the Rebels entered the final stretch of their playoff push last season, Kiffin is preparing for his first season in Baton Rouge under heavy expectations.

He has already brought in several highly regarded players through the transfer portal, and pursuing NFL returnees represents his latest attempt to strengthen LSU's roster and increase its playoff chances.

According to PFN's CFB Playoff Meter , LSU currently has a 31.7% chance of reaching the CFP this season.

articles.title: NFL, Roger Goodell have good reasons to quickly rule on Jed York punishment | Opinion
articles.summary: The NFL conduct policy says owners are held to a "higher standard." Jed York's arrest and plea deal will test that.
articles.body:
ATLANTA – NFL owners zipped into town on Wednesday and handled their business with all the efficiency of a two-minute drill.

They unanimously approved the sale of the Seattle Seahawks to Vinod, Neeru and Neal Khosla for a record $9.6 billion. They punted the Pro Bowl . They instituted a three-strikes policy that, in the name of safety, will result in an automatic one-game suspension for three violations of the most egregious penalties. They announced a new Behavioral Health Network to be launched in conjunction with the NFL Players Association to beef up mental health resources.

The whole meeting took less than four hours. They checked the boxes, then bolted.

Now, if Roger Goodell can only operate with such speed in closing the case on disgraced San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York that suddenly landed on his desk this week.

York, 46, pleaded no contest to two misdemeanor charges – plea-bargained down from an initial charge of "engaging in prostitution" – after an arrest at a trailer park in East Palestine, Ohio, on Sunday.

No, York wasn't among the owners seen on site at the special session.

49ers owner Jed York arrested. Revisit his years with the team

Coincidentally, the police bodycam footage of York's arrest , obtained by The California Post, dropped about the time his fellow owners were winding down their meetings late in the afternoon. USA TODAY Sports has also requested a copy of the footage.

And when the NFL Commissioner met with reporters for a brief gaggle after the meetings – which allowed owners to escape without much, if any, media interaction – the first question was about York. Goodell is determining the expected discipline coming for York under a conduct policy that purportedly holds owners to a "higher standard" than players and others in the NFL universe.

"It's being reviewed under the personal conduct policy," Goodell said. "We will do that. When there's something to be reported, we'll do so."

Of course, no decision on York – who on the police video appeared shocked and was docile without any resistance as he was handcuffed – was expected on Wednesday that would have taken shine off the christening of the newest members of the NFL owners club. And anyway, it's typical for Goodell to not say anything more than a basic acknowledgement in sticky situations like this.

Still, it's worth nothing that Goodell handed the late Jim Irsay a six-game suspension and $500,000 fine on the very day in 2014 that the Indianapolis Colts owner pleaded guilty to driving while intoxicated. In Irsay's case, it took more than six months for the court case to be resolved, allowing Goodell ample time to consider discipline in the interim.

In York's case, it came so fast – at least as it pertains to the arrest, plea bargain, one day in lock-up and widespread humiliation.

Now, with the legal case quickly resolved, Goodell needs to quickly decide on the level of discipline, and not only so it won't hang over York's franchise as it makes the long trek to Australia for one of the NFL's showcase international games in Week 1.

No, as coach Kyle Shanahan maintained, York's situation doesn't tangibly affect the football mission. Fred Warner will still chase down ball-carriers, sideline-to-sideline. Christian McCaffrey will still sting defenses via the ground or air. George Kittle is still, well, that baddie dude.

Yet striking closure will be good for the optics of the team – and a league that is always dealing with one fire or another.

Then there's another reason: compassion for York.

For everything that has happened fast, I'd suspect that whatever issues that exist in his life that led him to the predicament that came wrapped with his arrest, didn't happen overnight. If discipline involves time away from the team in the form of a suspension – and this helps in dealing with matters that have nothing to do with football – perhaps it will be a blessing in disguise for York.

After all, no punishment from Goodell may be harsher for York than the humiliation.

articles.title: Commanders' rookie earning major praise from top NFL analyst
articles.summary: NFL Insider Brian Baldinger breaks down what he calls the 'best catch' in preseason Week two from Washington Commanders' Jaden Bradley.
articles.body:
After the free agency frenzy and chaos of the NFL Draft died down, many NFL teams continued to add players to their rosters. The Washington Commanders signed nine undrafted rookie free agents after the draft was done, and a handful of them have made a legitimate case to remain on the final 53-man roster when the time comes.

One player attempting to make a case for himself is wide receiver Jaden Bradley. NFL Insider and analyst Brian Baldinger breaks down one of Bradley's receptions in the Commanders' loss to the Detroit Lions on Saturday.

"Trying to make a football team as an undrafted free agent like Jaden Bradley right here, from the slot," Baldiner begins. "Spray fade right here, all right? And you come down with this kind of a catch right in front of the bench, in front of Dan Quinn, in front of Jayden Daniels , like guys jumping up and down, celebrating the catch right there. That's cool. Antonio Williams , the rookie wide receiver, joining him.

"And watch this throw right here. Jaden Bradley is from DeMatha High School; he's a local product. Good blitz pickup here, by the way. Kaliakmanis lets it fly, and watch this catch; this is the best catch I've seen in the second week of preseason so far. That's how you get people's attention. That's how you make the team. That's how you get noticed as an undrafted free agent. Look at Terry McLaurin right here, coming down to celebrate with the rookie free agent. That's cool. I like that."

Bradley caught two passes for 42 yards against the Lions, an average of 21 yards per reception. One thing Baldinger didn't mention in his analysis is that, on top of it being an excellent catch, Bradley was also being held by the defender. If you watch the second showing of the play, you can see Bradley's left arm being held back by his opponent. And he still made the catch.

The Commanders' wide receiver room is pretty packed. There are only a couple of players who are locks to make the final roster, and the last couple of spots are up for grabs. If Bradley continues to perform at this level during the week and in the final preseason game against the Baltimore Ravens , his chances increase. Even if he doesn't make the Commanders' final roster, Bradley could very easily find himself on another team before the regular season begins. He was impressive during OTAs, the minicamp, and throughout training camp. He's worked after practice frequently with McLaurin.

In Washington's first preseason game, Bradley almost blocked multiple punts, showing he's willing to do whatever it takes to make the roster.

articles.title: NFL Players Who Should Consider Taking Advantage of New CFB Eligibility Rules
articles.summary: Several NFL players are set to make history as the first group to go through an NFL offseason and return to college.
articles.body:
Several NFL players are set to make history as the first group to go through an NFL offseason and return to college.

According to ESPN's Dan Murphy and Pete Thamel , a Louisiana state court granted several former Ole Miss players a temporary restraining order that allows them to return to college football for another season.

Tight end Dae'Quan Wright, defensive tackle Zxavian Harris and safety Wydett Williams Jr. are plaintiffs in a lawsuit against the NCAA. Wright signed with the Philadelphia Eagles and Cleveland Browns before Cleveland waived him on Aug. 24; the New Orleans Saints waived Harris on Aug. 8. Williams remains on the Arizona Cardinals' roster. All three played at Ole Miss last season.

The temporary restraining order permits the trio to play while the eligibility dispute proceeds.

As NCAA conferences move to bar players who have signed professional contracts from returning to college football, former NFL executive Andrew Brandt said he had heard of a few players asking their NFL teams to cut them sooner than expected so they could pursue a return to college.

"Now hearing of a few players going to their NFL teams and asking to be cut now (instead of likely being cut in two weeks) to go play in college again," he said. "What a time this is."

According to ESPN's Adam Schefter , the NFL has clarified that a player who signs an NFL contract and is later cut becomes a free agent after clearing waivers. The player may sign with another NFL team, join the CFL or return to college, but cannot re-enter a future NFL draft.

With all that in mind, here are six players who should take advantage of the fifth-year collegiate eligibility ruling. All of these players are long shots to make NFL rosters.

The Denver Broncos added Dallen Bentley to a crowded tight end room. This offseason, they re-signed Adam Trautman and Nate Adkins. In April, Denver drafted Justin Joly and Bentley in the fifth and seventh rounds, respectively. Evan Engram leads the group.

Despite a breakout 2025 collegiate year, hauling in 48 passes for 620 yards and six touchdowns, Bentley still has room for growth as a pass-catcher.

Bleacher Report scout Daniel Harms noted Bentley needed to improve in the nuances of playing the position in a receiving role.

" Bentley struggles to defeat man coverage and lacks the short-area quickness, consistent physicality, and route nuance to shake defenders. Has the size and frame to dig out defenders as a blocker, but needs to refine his hand placement, pad level, and power to do so ."

Bentley should consider returning to the collegiate level to further refine his skill set and build on his productive 2025 campaign at Utah.

The Green Bay Packers entered the offseason with a glaring need at cornerback. They released Nate Hobbs, signed Benjamin St-Juste and drafted Brandon Cisse and Domani Jackson.

As a second-round pick, Cisse will have opportunities to play in his rookie year. Jackson may not make the 53-man roster in part because he's missed extensive time.

The Athletic's Matt Schneidman explained why he didn't include Jackson in the Packers' cornerback room in his most recent 53-man depth chart projection.

" Jackson, the former Alabama and USC corner, has the advantage of being a recent draft pick, but the rookie sixth-rounder has been behind the eight ball after offseason core muscle surgery and just made his preseason debut. The Packers also have four outside corners above him on the depth chart ."

Jackson played at powerhouse collegiate programs, but he posted pedestrian coverage numbers. With another year in college, the 6'0", 194-pound defensive back could develop into more of a playmaker.

On a roster in desperate need of running back help, Jam Miller may have been able to work his way into a backfield rotation. He's earned praise from head coach Mike Vrabel for his preseason debut performance.

" It was good to see Jam come out and have some nice runs. I felt like he ran with his pads down and had a couple physical runs, and was happy for him. This is a great evaluation. We can start to figure out guys that can and start to figure out guys that can't, too ."

Miller finished that game with 14 carries for 55 yards. He followed up with 11 rush attempts for 36 yards against the Philadelphia Eagles last week.

However, New England may favor special teams veteran Hassan Haskins for the No. 3 running back spot behind Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson. Keep in mind that he played under Vrabel with the Tennessee Titans in 2022.

With experience running against NFL defenders, Miller could have a true breakout collegiate season. He led Alabama's ground attack in 2025 but logged 130 carries for 504 yards and three touchdowns. Rather than remain on the practice squad, the 5'10", 209-pound ball-carrier could raise his stock with another strong year on his college resume.

Players Who'll Make or Break Fantasy Teams

The Kansas City Chiefs revamped their running back room, signing Kenneth Walker and Emari Demercado and selecting Emmett Johnson in the fifth round of the draft. They also signed Jaydn Ott, who went undrafted.

Given the veteran talent on the Chiefs' running back depth chart, Johnson's productive preseason and Brashard Smith in his second season with the team, Ott has an uphill climb to make the roster.

Ott has had a modest showing in the preseason, recording two receptions for 40 yards without a carry. The 23-year-old should consider another year in the collegiate ranks, where he can rack up far better numbers than in his 2025 campaign as a backup at Oklahoma.

After a promising 2023 collegiate term at California, when he logged 246 rush attempts for 1,315 yards and 12 touchdowns, Ott recorded 137 carries for 443 yards and four scores over the previous two years with the Golden Bears and Sooners.

If Ott earns a lead role in a return to college, he could have a better chance at an NFL roster spot following a standout year.

Three teams have signed Kobe Prentice over the course of the offseason, but he's unlikely to make it through roster cuts because of constant movement across the league at a crucial time for rookies.

The Carolina Panthers signed Prentice after he went undrafted. In July, they waived him two days after the start of their training camp program. The New England Patriots claimed the 22-year-old off waivers, and he had a chance to make an impression.

In two preseason games, Prentice hauled in four of his seven targets for 47 yards, but the Patriots waived him after their second exhibition contest.

The New York Giants claimed Prentice, but he's a long shot to secure a roster spot, even though the team lost wideout Calvin Austin III for the 2026 season because of a serious knee injury.

Barring an all-time performance in Big Blue's preseason finale, Prentice won't be able to make up ground on the other wideouts who have been with the team over the summer. In Austin's absence, Darnell Mooney and rookie third-rounder Malachi Fields will likely have key roles alongside Malik Nabers (when healthy) and Darius Slayton. On the roster bubble, Odell Beckham Jr. could hang around.

Prentice played through three collegiate campaigns at Alabama before transferring to Baylor. With his modest receiving numbers in college, another year could help boost his free-agent market value on a fourth try with another NFL team in 2027.

The Buffalo Bills selected Toriano Pride Jr. with their first of three seventh-round picks. At 5'10", 185 pounds, he projects as a slot defender on the pro level, though the rookie has seen time on the boundary in the preseason.

Pride plays with enough physicality to be a nickelback on the pro level, but the Bills replaced Taron Johnson with Dee Alford.

Assuming defensive back C.J. Gardner-Johnson is ready for the season after dealing with a calf strain, he can also line up in the slot. A fifth-rounder from last year's draft, Jordan Hancock could play the role as well. He suited up for 13 games last season.

Typically, backup nickelbacks don't see much time on the field. So, Pride would need to convince the Bills that he could thrive on the boundary. ESPN's Alaina Getzenberg left him off her latest Bills 53-man depth chart projection.

If the Bills cut Pride, he could return to college to boost his resume as a versatile playmaker.

articles.title: 8 Players Who Will Make or Break Fantasy Football Rosters in 2026
articles.summary: With less than two weeks remaining before the 2026 NFL season kicks off, fantasy managers have two major draft weekends left before the New England Patriots visit the Seattle Seahawks on September 9.
articles.body:
With less than two weeks remaining before the 2026 NFL season kicks off, fantasy managers have two major draft weekends left before the New England Patriots visit the Seattle Seahawks on September 9.

It's time to move on from last season's championship win and time to relegate that 2-12 campaign from a year ago to the dustbin of history.

As always, the first step toward fantasy glory is having a successful draft.

Success on draft day is about finding value and avoiding busts: selecting players who can outperform their ADP while steering clear of those unlikely to justify their cost. Getting those decisions right can make a fantasy season; getting them wrong can just as easily derail one.

QB Trevor Lawrence, Jacksonville Jaguars

That quarterbacks like Trevor Lawrence of the Jacksonville Jaguars are available as late as they are goes a long way toward explaining why so many veteran fantasy drafters play chicken at the position and wait to select a starter.

Last year, Lawrence topped 4,000 passing yards, threw a career-high 29 touchdown passes, added nine scores on the ground and finished the season fourth in fantasy points among quarterbacks.

Perhaps even more importantly, Lawrence was the highest-scoring fantasy signal-caller down the stretch last season, as Andy Smith noted for RotoBaller :

"From Weeks 12 through 18, Lawrence averaged an elite 29.5 PPR points per game while scoring 22 touchdowns (18 through the air) and averaging 265.1 passing yards per game. During this stretch, Lawrence was the QB1 by a wide margin, sitting nearly four points per game above Josh Allen. In terms of passing scores, Lawrence's 18 trailed only Matthew Stafford by one, but his 22 total TDs led the position. As the season progressed, Lawrence showed significant development under the Liam Coen system. Now with a full season under his belt, Lawrence could very well maintain this pace over the course of a full season."

Projecting Lawrence to be the No. 1 quarterback overall may be a reach—those nine rushing touchdowns aren't going to be easy to duplicate. But he is playing in a loaded offense for a coach who has produced top-five fantasy quarterbacks in back-to-back years.

There's no question that Joe Burrow of the Cincinnati Bengals is a fantastic NFL quarterback.

Just two years ago, he led the league in pass attempts, completions, passing yards and passing touchdowns. He has arguably the best one-two punch at wide receiver in the league in Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins.

Burrow told reporters he has one goal this year—to get back to the Super Bowl:

"I'm trying to put it out in the world; I'm trying to manifest it. I'm trying to show our guys the urgency that I have, and that I want us to have as an organization to go and make it happen. You can keep pushing it down the road, or you can talk about it now and say this is the year. I'm tired of saying next year, next year, next year. This is it."

However, while Burrow has his sights set on a championship, he's not leading fantasy teams to one.

For starters, his injury history is a material concern. In six NFL seasons, he has missed at least six games three times, including over half the 2025 campaign. Cincinnati's offensive line is generally regarded as below-average , which doesn't help his chances of staying healthy.

Burrow offers limited rushing production, which raises the bar for his passing output at his current ADP. To return value, he likely will need to approach the elite passing production that made him the QB2 in fantasy points two seasons ago.

At his QB3 ADP, Burrow carries a price premium over Dak Prescott despite offering a similar fantasy profile.

Kyren Williams of the Los Angeles Rams is one of the more polarizing running backs in fantasy football in 2026.

Quite a few fantasy managers are skeptical that he can log another top-10 season, largely due to the emergence of Blake Corum over the second half of last year. In 2024, Williams logged 350 touches. Last year, that number dropped to 295.

However, there are also proponents of Williams like Jason Wood of Footballguys who counter that an increase in the quality of his touches more than compensates for a dip in quality:

"Williams is a classic case of market fatigue. Concerns over Blake Corum eating into Williams' value ignore the data: Corum's slight volume uptick in 2025 simply absorbed the snaps of fringe backups, while Williams delivered another top-8 fantasy campaign. With contract security, McVay's preference for a main back, and continued ownership of high-value touches, Williams is a fine selection at cost. He is a reliable starter who delivers steady RB1 production without requiring premium early-round draft capital."

He had more scrimmage yards (1,553) in fewer touches last year. He has over 1,100 rushing yards in three straight seasons. At least 13 touchdowns in three straight seasons. Top-10 PPR numbers in three straight seasons, and he tied a career-high with 5.2 yards per touch a year ago.

He's a fantastic draft-day target in Round 3 for managers who snag a pair of elite wide receivers in the first couple of rounds.

RB Christian McCaffrey, San Francisco 49ers

Last year, Christian McCaffrey of the San Francisco 49ers topped 2,000 total yards for the third time in his professional career. He topped 100 receptions for the third time in his career. No running back had more PPR points.

However, he also led all running backs with 413 total touches, so when he missed practice time recently some fantasy drafters started to rethink their strategy.

However, McCaffrey told reporters that the rest was all part of the plan to keep him fresh throughout the season:

"Obviously when you don't practice, the way the media works now, is a firestorm. This was kind of part of the plan from the jump—to ramp up pretty big, get nine or 10 practices in, kind of come back down and then ramp up again so we're fresh for the duration. "Sometimes I can probably be my own worst enemy in how much I love being out there. I want to run, I want to go. I want every play, I'm a competitor, I love it and I think when you have people smarter than you, that understand not just what you've been through, but what we plan on doing this season."

McCaffrey enters his age-30 season after handling 413 touches and surpassing 2,000 yards in 2025—an unusually demanding workload. He also missed 14 games in the seasons immediately following his two previous 2,000-yard campaigns, underscoring the durability risk at his current ADP.

As Footballguys noted, he is a leading candidate to disappoint fantasy managers in 2026.

No wide receiver in fantasy football is a bigger target for this writer than Denver Broncos wideout Jaylen Waddle.

And that was the case before this happened in the preseason:

Waddle was acquired by the Broncos in an offseason trade, and Adam Pfeifer of A Fantasy Life expects the sixth-year veteran to be a big part of the offense in Denver:

"There should also be a serious uptick in pass volume headed Waddle's way. This past season, despite claiming one of the elite defenses in football, the Broncos continued to rely on the pass. Denver ranked third in football in dropback rate over expected last season (4%), while their 57.8% neutral script pass rate since 2023 is the seventh-highest mark in the league. Quarterback Bo Nix led the NFL in pass attempts a season ago with 612, averaging 36 per contest. Stout defense or not, the Broncos want to throw the football. And my guess? They want to throw it to Waddle. A lot."

As a rookie in 2021, Waddle caught 104 passes. He followed that with 1,356 receiving yards in 2022 and led the NFL with 18.1 yards per reception.

The 27-year-old is going to be the No. 1 wideout in Denver this year. Career highs in receptions and receiving yards are in play, and he is going to be a top-10 fantasy option.

And with an ADP in the middle of Round 4, Waddle is going to win people leagues in 2026.

For the most part, the top 10 wideouts in fantasy drafts are a relatively safe lot. They may not finish in the order they are drafted, but the bust risk with elite pass-catchers is relatively low.

This isn't about Drake London as a player—the fifth-year veteran was fourth in PPR points among receivers in 2024 and eighth in PPR points per game last year.

However, there's likely to be a new quarterback in Atlanta this year (at least to start)—and that's a problem, according to Matt LaMarca of Fantasy Labs :

"While Tagovailoa may well end up being an upgrade for the Falcons overall, it's possible that it's a significant downgrade for London specifically. Tagovailoa doesn't have the same caliber of arm, so he's going to have to rely on short-to-intermediate throws. We saw that in his preseason debut, where four of his five pass attempts were directed towards Kyle Pitts. In addition to Pitts, London also has to share the field with one of the best running backs in football. Bijan Robinson can do it all. He's obviously a major threat on the ground, but he's also a phenomenal pass-catcher. He posted a 20% target share, which was tied for the second-highest mark at running back last year."

That target share matched De'Von Achane's in Miami last season. Tagovailoa's quick-release, short-to-intermediate passing profile may not maximize London's downfield skill set.

If the Falcons rush Michael Penix Jr. back from an ACL tear, as has been speculated , that would help, but it carries issues of its own given the quarterback was only just cleared to practice fully.

Also, while London is immensely talented, he has also surpassed 1,000 yards just once in four years.

London isn't going to vanish, but he is unlikely to finish as a top-10 fantasy receiver in 2026.

Fantasy drafters essentially have three options at tight end this season: pay a premium for an elite option such as Las Vegas Raiders star Brock Bowers; wait for a Tier 2 player such as Atlanta's Kyle Pitts; or fade the position and target a late-round upside play.

If the third option sounds like your speed, then Juwan Johnson of the Saints should be on your target list.

Johnson is all but an afterthought in drafts this year, with an ADP in Round 12. But with rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson set to miss a chunk of the regular season, Brad Evans of The Athletic sees a path to top-five fantasy numbers for Johnson in 2026:

"The loss of Jordan Tyson for likely the first several weeks of the season is a swift midsection kick to a Saints offense that was moving in a positive direction. End-zone spikes have been infrequent for Johnson the past three years, but coming off career highs in receptions (77) and receiving yards (889), he shouldn't be overlooked. Keep in mind he also finished in the top seven at the position in air yards, yards after catch and expected fantasy points per game. With his target share likely to climb, he's sure to turn a tidy profit."

Those receptions and receiving yards both ranked inside the top five at the position, and from Week 10 on last year, he was seventh in PPR points per game among tight ends.

That's a bargain. Tack on another touchdown or three, and Johnson's a steal.

Every year in fantasy, there are players whose ADP befuddles me.

This year, Detroit Lions tight end Sam LaPorta is one of those players.

Yes, LaPorta is capable of posting elite fantasy numbers. As a rookie in 2023, he was targeted 120 times, catching 86 passes for 889 yards and 10 scores on the way to the top spot among fantasy tight ends.

In the two years since, though, the 25-year-old has 132 targets and 10 touchdowns.

That was partly due to injury, but as C.H. Herms noted for FTN , it's also because LaPorta plays in arguably the most crowded passing attack in the league:

"The Detroit Lions have several mouths to feed. It's an incredibly busy pride. LaPorta is great, sure, but so is Amon-Ra St. Brown. Speedster Jameson Williams is also probably going to have some hefty involvement after soaring to a career-high 95.2% route share last season. Hell, the Motor City maniacs just gave running back Jahmyr Gibbs a bag and a half to be the highest-paid running back per annual dough in the entire NFL! A very crowded scene, indeed."

For as talented as LaPorta is, he's at best the No. 3 option in Detroit's passing game. Injuries have been an issue each of the past two years, including eight missed games in 2025. A hip injury has already limited him over the summer.

LaPorta isn't a terrible pick—all the Tier 2 tight ends carry questions—but he's being drafted at his ceiling.

Drafting at ceiling is how fantasy seasons get broken.

Gary Davenport is a two-time Fantasy Sports Writers Association Football Writer of the Year. Follow Gary on X at @IDPGodfather .

Wait, not just any player, but an NFL quarterback? That’s a different story altogether.Because you represent an entire team. An entire city.And then you go out and pose like you’re just watching TV, or reportedly make an X user feel like, “MF is eye f*cking me through the phone.” That’s a whole other universe of a story.Maybe it was fine when it was limited to his colorful nail polish - not just black, goth-like, or one painted nail, but all colorful nails. But now, when you’re wearing an NFL rivalry uniform and seemingly showing the world, “Don’t look at the uniform; look at how I’m sitting” - we can’t even go there.No wonder it reportedly led fans to draw homophobic comparisons. Once it’s out there, there’s no stopping the comments. It will no longer be about the rivalry uniform. It will be about how you sat, what you felt while taking that photo, and how you’re projecting yourself to the world.Caleb Williams’ NFL rivalry uniform photoshoot sparks strong reactionsThe Chicago Bears unveiled their 2026 alternate navy and orange uniforms on August 25, set to debut on Christmas Day against their longtime rivals, the Green Bay Packers, at Soldier Field in Chicago, Illinois.Their star quarterback, Caleb Williams, posed in the uniform in a Nike photoshoot, striking studio poses that included sitting with one leg up and stretching. Only the first one was from the Bears’ official video showcasing the NFL rivalry uniforms. The other three appeared to be inspired by the first photo.Fans recognize AI generated Caleb Williams photosThe seemingly AI-generated images showed Williams in several compromising poses. articles.title: How Patrick Mahomes’ $504M fortune is powering his billionaire ambitions with a growing sports empire
articles.summary: NFL News: Patrick Mahomes has already built one of the most decorated careers in modern football, but his ambitions reach far beyond the Kansas City Chiefs. The.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes has already built one of the most decorated careers in modern football, but his ambitions reach far beyond the Kansas City Chiefs. The superstar quarterback has used his NFL earnings, endorsement power and competitive instincts to build a growing portfolio of investments. From professional sports teams to wellness companies and real estate, Mahomes is steadily creating a business empire that could push his wealth toward billionaire territory.Patrick Mahomes is building a powerful sports investment portfolioMahomes' approach to wealth has been different from simply collecting endorsement checks. He has put his money into businesses and sports franchises that allow him to remain connected to industries he genuinely follows.His love for baseball runs deep. His father, Pat Mahomes Sr., enjoyed a lengthy MLB career, and Patrick was even selected by the Detroit Tigers in the 2014 MLB Draft. He never signed with the organization, choosing football instead, but baseball remained part of his world.That connection later helped lead Mahomes into ownership. He became a minority investor in the Kansas City Royals and also took stakes in other Kansas City sports ventures, including Sporting Kansas City. His involvement in women's soccer has further expanded his presence in the city's sporting community.Formula One has also caught his attention. Mahomes joined an investment group connected to Alpine, alongside fellow athletes and business figures. Speaking about the opportunity, he said:“I think everybody can see the appeal.“I’ve been able to get to a couple races now, seeing the environment, and then obviously watching the Drive to Survive on Netflix you see how competitive it is.“Any time you get an opportunity to get in on that, I mean I’m as competitive as anyone can get, so hopefully it can open up to some great opportunities and we are able to go to some of those races and have a little stake in the game.”That quote captures something important about Mahomes' strategy. He is not only buying into sports. He is looking for opportunities where his personal interests and competitive mindset can translate into long-term business value.Patrick Mahomes' endorsements and investments add another layerPatrick Mahomes NFL contract remains a major foundation of his fortune. He signed a reworked 8-year, $504.75 million contract extension with the Kansas City Chiefs in June 2026, making it the first half-billion-dollar deal in NFL history.Adidas has given him a signature line, while major brands including State Farm, Subway, Oakley and Head & Shoulders have used his image. He has also been involved with Prime, the beverage company associated with Logan Paul and KSI.But Mahomes has increasingly moved beyond traditional advertising. His investments have included wellness and technology companies such as Whoop, while his equity partnership with Hyperice has given him a stake in a recovery-focused business.Real estate adds another asset class to the picture. His property holdings have included a Texas mansion and a Kansas City condo, giving the quarterback yet another way to diversify his wealth.The bigger story is not simply how much Mahomes earns. It is how deliberately he appears to be putting that money to work. His football career provides the cash flow, his celebrity creates access, and his investments give him opportunities that can continue growing long after his playing days end.For Mahomes, becoming a billionaire may still be a distant target.
