articles.title: Travis Kelce’s alleged $12.9M donation to help homeless families exposed as a completely fabricated story
articles.summary: NFL News: A viral story portraying Travis Kelce as a major force in the fight against homelessness has once again made its way across social media. The claim so.
articles.body: A viral story portraying Travis Kelce as a major force in the fight against homelessness has once again made its way across social media. The claim sounds inspiring, but it is not true. Snopes has rated the story false, finding no credible evidence that the Kansas City Chiefs star donated $12.9 million in bonuses and endorsements to build homes for people experiencing homelessness.Travis Kelce $12.9 million donation claim falls apartThe Facebook posts claimed Kelce had donated his “entire” $12.9 million in bonuses and endorsements to an organization called the Homeless Housing Initiative. According to the posts, the money would fund 150 homes containing 300 beds.The story also included an emotional statement supposedly delivered by Kelce at a press conference:“I witnessed the impact of homelessness firsthand as a child, and I knew that if I ever had the means, I would make a meaningful contribution,” Travis Kelce said at a press conference. “No one deserves to sleep on the streets.”There was one major problem. No credible record of Kelce making those remarks could be found.Snopes reported that searches for the supposed quote produced no reliable news coverage. That matters because a public announcement involving millions of dollars and a major construction project would normally attract substantial attention from sports and mainstream news outlets.The alleged charity also raised another red flag. Snopes found no listing for the Homeless Housing Initiative in Charity Navigator, adding to the evidence that the organization described in the viral posts was not legitimate.The posts gained considerable traction, with several identical versions collecting tens of thousands of reactions. Their popularity, however, did not make the claim any more credible.Travis Kelce charity work is real, but this story is notThe false donation story is particularly convincing because Kelce has an established record of charitable work. He has used his platform to support causes through his Eighty-Seven and Running Foundation, making it easy for a fabricated story to appear believable.Kelce himself addressed a similar false story on the April 9, 2025, episode of his “New Heights” podcast. While discussing the real work of his foundation, he pushed back against fabricated reports circulating online.“This time I wasn't doing what was falsely claimed by the social channels or the outlets posting all this AI stuff,” Kelce said.The financial details in the latest rumor also do not fit Kelce's known earnings. Forbes reported that Kelce was making about $30 million from endorsements in 2025. He and his brother, Jason Kelce, also signed a three-year, $100 million deal with Wondery for their “New Heights” podcast in 2024.That does not prove that Kelce would never make a donation of this size. It does show why the specific $12.9 million figure deserves scrutiny.There are genuine examples of NFL players helping people facing homelessness. Former NFL player Jordan Jenkins bought two duplexes and donated them to The Plummer Home to help house homeless veterans. Warrick Dunn has also spent years providing homes to families through his charitable foundation.Those real efforts highlight the key lesson behind the Kelce rumor. A heartwarming story can spread quickly, but generosity should be verified rather than assumed. In this case, the viral claim about Travis Kelce donating $12.9 million and funding 150 homes was simply not supported by the evidence.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: DK Metcalf Reportedly Restructures Steelers Contract, Updated Salary Cap for 2026 NFL Season
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers have reportedly quintupled their 2026 cap space by reworking wide receiver DK Metcalf's contract.
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers have reportedly quintupled their 2026 cap space by reworking wide receiver DK Metcalf's contract.

The Steelers restructured Metcalf's deal to create almost $18 million in cap space next season, ESPN's Field Yates reported Thursday.

Report: Seahawks All-Pro DT Gets $90M Deal

The move was made by converting Metcalf's base salary into a signing bonus.

The Steelers ranked 32nd in the NFL with just $3.78 million in Top 51 cap space prior to the move, per Spotrac .

The contract readjustment reported by Yates could take the Steelers to around $21 million in cap space, which Spotrac estimates would rank around 15th in the league.

Metcalf, acquired from the Seattle Seahawks ahead of the 2025 season and extended immediately afterward, is currently signed through the 2029 season.

He was previously set to play the 2027 campaign with a $32.5 million cap hit, which Spotrac reports broke down into a $20 million base salary, $6 million signing bonus and $6.5 million roster bonus.

The news comes amid ongoing contract negotiations with cornerback Joey Porter Jr. Head coach Mike McCarthy recently said the team and Porter are at an "impasse."

Porter, who was placed on the PUP list in July with a reported back injury, was one of the most effective pieces of the Steelers' defense last season. He allowed just a 56.2 passer rating when targeted by other quarterbacks in 2025, per PFF .

NFL Network's Ian Rapoport recently reported Porter could be looking at cashing in on that campaign by becoming the NFL's highest-paid cornerback.

The top of the cornerback market sits around $30 million, per Over the Cap . Devon Witherspoon currently leads the positional rankings thanks to his $33 million average annual salary with the Seattle Seahawks.

Clearing out salary cap space could potentially help the Steelers end the contract stalemate before the regular season, during which the franchise typically does not negotiate new contracts.

The Steelers won't be the only team impacted by the potential resolution of these contract talks. Should Porter re-sign with Pittsburgh before the start of the season, other clubs in the market for a cornerback may have to turn elsewhere to bolster their secondary via trade.

articles.title: Fantasy Football 2026 Preseason Mock Draft Strategy, Rankings and Analysis
articles.summary: Fantasy football managers are officially on the clock.
articles.body:
Fantasy football managers are officially on the clock.

Or up against the clock, rather. With the 2026 NFL season kicking off on Wednesday, Sept 9., it'll probably be a little while longer before managers are actually on the clock and needing to submit their selections.

Still, that only leaves so much time to finalize rankings, build a draft blueprint and then hit the mock draft rooms to take that strategy on a few test runs. This should help keep things moving as we're laying out the first three rounds of a mock draft, updated PPR rankings and some strategic tips for acing your draft.

The NFL is a pass-happy league with a lot of committee-style backfields. High-volume featured backs have never felt in less supply and should therefore rank pretty high on your demand list.

A bellcow back can help elevate both your floor and your ceiling. That role effectively locks in solid production from week-to-week, and the talent helps deliver those spectacular weeks that may well decide your matchups. While you never want to reach to fill a positional need, the draft board should allow you to feel good about using either your first- or second-round pick (or even both) on a top-shelf running back.

Don't pay a premium at quarterback or tight end.

In most league formats, you'll often find yourself starting as many as six players who are either running backs or receivers (the sixth spot being your flex). You'll also typically wind up playing just one quarterback and one tight end.

Clearly, then, you need as much talent at running back and receiver as you can find. And since those are priority positions for effectively everyone at the top of the draft, that means there is a massive opportunity cost should you spend an early pick on either a quarterback or receiver.

The juice just isn't worth the squeeze. Especially when the fantasy gap between great quarterbacks or tight ends and good ones isn't as wide as what you'll find at running back and receiver. You can work the waiver wire for streaming options at quarterback or tight end if you need to, but you'll be hurting if you're trying to plug-and-play a running back or receiver off the scrap heap.

articles.title: Rams' Puka Nacua Named to NFL Top 100, Check Out the Updated 2026 Rankings

Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua ended up seventh overall on the annual NFL Top 100 as the final names of the player-voted list continued to drop on Thursday.

Nacua jumped 34 spots from No. 41 on last year's list.

articles.title: New Alec Pierce Injury Update, Timeline to Return for Colts After Being Activated off PUP
articles.summary: The Indianapolis Colts activated wide receiver Alec Pierce from the physically unable to perform list on Thursday, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter and Fox59's Mike Chappell.
articles.body:
The Indianapolis Colts activated wide receiver Alec Pierce from the physically unable to perform list on Thursday, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter and Fox59's Mike Chappell .

Per Schefter, the Colts' plan is to "start ramping up" Pierce's activity in hopes that he will be ready for the team's regular-season opener against the Baltimore Ravens on Sept. 13.

Pierce underwent ankle surgery in March, and he had been on the PUP list since the start of training camp last month.

Originally selected by Indianapolis in the second round of the 2022 NFL draft, Pierce enjoyed a breakout season in 2024, recording 37 receptions for 824 yards and a career-high seven touchdowns.

He followed that up with an even better 2025 campaign, setting career highs with 47 grabs for 1,003 yards, while also scoring six touchdowns.

Pierce has led the NFL in yards per catch in each of the past two seasons, topping 21 yards per reception both times.

Given Pierce's status as the Colts' top deep threat and their leading receiver in terms of yardage last season, the organization went to great lengths to keep him in the fold.

The Colts signed Pierce to a four-year, $114 million contract in free agency, giving him an average annual salary of $28.5 million.

Pierce's importance to the Colts' 2026 success became even greater on March 13 when Indianapolis traded wideout Michael Pittman Jr. to the Pittsburgh Steelers.

Pittman was the Colts' most consistent receiving threat during his six seasons in Indianapolis with 485 receptions for 5,254 yards.

Re-signing Pierce and trading Pittman was seemingly a vote of confidence by the Colts in Pierce being able to become a true, No. 1 wideout.

If Pierce is not ready for Week 1, then Josh Downs and recently signed veteran Keenan Allen figure to be quarterback Daniel Jones' top targets at wide receiver, along with second-year tight end Tyler Warren.

Tillman has flashed at times during his career. Over a three-game stretch (Weeks 7-9) in 2024, Tillman caught 21 passes for 255 yards and three touchdowns. He also began the 2025 season with a five-catch, 52-yard, one-touchdown performance against the Cincinnati Bengals.

The 6'3", 215-pound Tillman certainly presents a big target for quarterbacks, and it's certainly possible he lands somewhere soon enough. The cutdown day is 6 p.m. ET on Sunday, when NFL teams have to get down to 53 players.

articles.title: Leonard Williams, Seahawks Reportedly Agree to $90M Contract Extension After Witherspoon Deal
articles.summary: Having already handed out lucrative contract extensions to Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Devon Witherspoon, the Seattle Seahawks aren't done yet.
articles.body:
Having already handed out lucrative contract extensions to Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Devon Witherspoon, the Seattle Seahawks aren't done yet.

According to ESPN and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , defensive tackle Leonard Williams and the Seahawks agreed to terms on a three-year, $90 million contract on Thursday. The deal includes $56 million guaranteed, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter .

ESPN's Jeremy Fowler first reported the sides were nearing an agreement.

Talks between Williams and the Seahawks have been ongoing for some time. He confirmed at the start of training camp last month that the two sides have been engaged in "conversations" without suggesting any timeline for a deal to get done.

"There's been a few conversations," he said on July 28, "but nothing set in stone."

Williams' current three-year, $64.5 million contract was set to expire at the end of the 2026 season. He originally signed that deal in March 2024, five months after the Seahawks acquired him in a trade from the New York Giants.

The $30 million average annual salary on Williams' new deal matches the value of Vita Vea's one-year extension he signed with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Aug. 19.

Williams is now one of six interior defensive linemen making at least $30 million per season. He joins a group that includes Vea, Jalen Carter, Quinnen Williams, Jeffery Simmons and Chris Jones.

In two full seasons playing in head coach Mike Macdonald's system, Williams has put together arguably the best stretch of his career. He has recorded 50 quarterback hits, 25 tackles for loss and 18 sacks in 33 games since the start of the 2024 campaign.

There's certainly risk on the Seahawks' part in giving a deal at this value to a player entering his age-32 season, but his performance suggests he can play at a high level for at least most of this contract.

The Seahawks allowed the fewest points in the NFL last season en route to winning the Super Bowl. Williams' presence in the middle of the defensive line helped unlock the entire unit, so it's only fitting he would be rewarded for his efforts with a new deal.

Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson compared the hands of rookie wide receiver Ja'Kobi Lane, who has drawn rave reviews this offseason, to those of Odell Beckham Jr. and DeAndre Hopkins when ESPN's Jamison Hensley asked him what it's like throwing the ball to the ex-USC star.

"[Ja'Kobi Lane] is [an] easy target," Jackson said. "Big guy—like 6'4", 6'5"—[he can] catch the ball with the best of them. I told you, my comparison [is] like Odell Beckham Jr. and DeAndre Hopkins with the hands."

It's not hard to find Lane training camp highlights or people raving about his work.

It's certainly conceivable Lane slides into the WR3 spot behind Zay Flowers and Rashod Bateman at this point.

The Ravens selected the 6'4", 205-pound Lane with the 80th overall pick in this year's NFL draft. He was a starter over his final two USC seasons (2024-2025), amassing a total of 92 catches for 1,270 yards and 16 touchdowns.

Now it appears Lane will get his fair share of opportunities right away in Baltimore as the Ravens look to get new head coach Jesse Minter's era off to a good start.

articles.title: Bill Belichick: European franchise a question for the NFL, says legendary coach
articles.summary: Six-time Super Bowl winning head coach Bill Belichick says the possibility of a European franchise is a question for the NFL.
articles.body:
Six-time Super Bowl winning head coach Bill Belichick says the possibility of a European franchise is a question for the NFL, but welcomes the global expansion of American football.

NFL fixtures regularly take place across Europe throughout the season and there also has an international pathway for players, but all 32 franchises are in the United States.

Belichick was speaking in Dublin before the American College Classic on Saturday (17:00 BST) between his North Carolina Tar Heels side and the Texas Christian University, which is the opening round of the season.

The 74-year-old - regarded as one of the greatest coaches of all time - took over as head coach of UNC in 2025 after a glittering 23 years with the New England Patriots in the NFL, where he won six Super Bowls.

When asked if he felt a European franchise was feasible or if it was something he would want to see happen, Belichick said it was "a question for the NFL and commissioner [Roger] Goodell".

"The NFL is very intent on building a global brand and you can see that in their scheduling this year," he said.

"Every time I've been part of those international games, the enthusiasm and the excitement is tremendous.

"I'm sure the NFL will continue to pursue that. College football is doing it with this game, so I think it is great for the game."

Belichick 'wisdom' guiding UNC on Dublin trip

Belichick highlighted that the possibility of the Jacksonville Jaguars relocating to London and Wembley had been explored in the past, but they ultimately stayed put and built their own new stadium in Florida.

He did, however, believe the travel involved would not stop a franchise being developed in Europe.

"It would certainly be a little bit of an adjustment coming here, but it's not a whole lot different than coming from the east coast to the west coast in the USA," Belichick added.

"Time-wise it's a long trip, but going from New York or Boston or Philly to LA or Seattle, it's about the same."

After 23 years in the NFL, Belichick said it was "important" for him to give back to the sport that "has been good to me and my family".

"American football is a great game, fans around the world love it.

"There's not a lot of it being played outside of the US, but I know when I visited places like Croatia or Germany there are a lot of local teams who play in their own leagues.

"It's super-popular. Anything I can do to give back to the game, whether that is in our country or internationally, I want to be part of that and I want to do it."

When asked if he would ever return to the NFL in a coaching capacity, Belichick said his full focus was on North Carolina.

"I recruited these kids and I want to help them," he added.

"I had a great experience in the NFL but I'm very happy to be at North Carolina and I'm excited about the future of our programme."

articles.summary: NFL News: Former Philadelphia Eagles running back Miles Sanders was arrested on DUI and careless driving charges in June after police found him slumped over in .
articles.body: Former Philadelphia Eagles running back Miles Sanders was arrested on DUI and careless driving charges in June after police found him slumped over in the driver’s seat of a Lexus stopped in the middle of William Penn Highway in Churchill Borough, Pennsylvania. According to CBS Pittsburgh, the 29-year-old was found in and out of consciousness and could not answer officers’ questions. Police said he later performed poorly on field sobriety tests and tested positive for alcohol. A package of suspected marijuana was also found inside the vehicle, according to court records. Sanders is due back in court in September. His attorney, Phil DiLucente, said the case has not reached the preliminary hearing stage and declined to comment further.Miles Sanders was found slumped over in a car on a Pennsylvania highwayThe arrest happened on June 8 in Churchill Borough, about 10 miles outside Pittsburgh. Police were called after a vehicle was reported sitting still in the middle of William Penn Highway near Beulah Road. When an officer reached the Lexus, Sanders was reportedly slumped over in the driver’s seat.According to the criminal complaint reported by CBS Pittsburgh, officers made several attempts to wake him. Police said Sanders appeared to be “in and out of consciousness” and “extremely lethargic,” while also saying he could not answer their questions. When he got out of the car, officers said his eyes looked glossy and his breath smelled of alcohol. Police also said Sanders admitted that he had been drinking earlier that day.Sanders then took field sobriety tests, and police said he performed poorly. A portable breath test also showed a positive result for alcohol, according to the complaint. Officers arrested him and charged him with driving under the influence of alcohol or a controlled substance and careless driving. Police also reported finding a package of suspected marijuana inside the vehicle.Miles Sanders’ NFL career now meets a new legal issueThe arrest comes as Sanders remains a free agent after last playing for the Dallas Cowboys in 2025. Before that, he spent four seasons with the Eagles, who selected him in the second round of the 2019 NFL Draft out of Penn State. Sanders made the Pro Bowl in 2022 and later signed with the Carolina Panthers before joining Dallas.His 2025 season ended early after he played in four games for the Cowboys. CBS Pittsburgh reported that his last NFL appearance came on September 28, 2025, against the Green Bay Packers. Sanders has 4,462 rushing yards and 24 rushing touchdowns across 88 NFL games, along with 183 catches for 1,274 yards and four receiving touchdowns.Sanders is scheduled to return to court in September, according to court records. articles.title: Cedric Tillman: His rise gave fans hope, his struggles raised doubts, and his brutal end broke both
articles.summary: NFL News: The Cleveland Browns have released wide receiver Cedric Tillman, per ESPN's Adam Schefter, as the NFL's 53-man roster deadline closes in. The move was.
articles.body: The Cleveland Browns have released wide receiver Cedric Tillman, per ESPN's Adam Schefter, as the NFL's 53-man roster deadline closes in. The move was not entirely shocking. Cleveland spent the 2026 draft capital loading up at receiver, bringing in rookies KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston while keeping Jerry Jeudy and Isaiah Bond locked in. That left little room for Tillman, who never quite seized his moment in three seasons with the Browns. Now free, he enters the market at an interesting time, and Kansas City may be paying close attention.Why did the Browns release Cedric Tillman before the 53-man deadline?Tillman's release traces back to a simple numbers problem. Cleveland selected him in the third round of the 2023 NFL Draft, 74th overall, with the expectation that the former Tennessee standout would develop into a reliable option. Over 38 games and three seasons, he caught 71 passes for 833 yards and five touchdowns. Last year, he contributed 21 receptions for 270 yards and two scores across 13 games. Serviceable production. But not enough to hold off a younger, more hyped crop of pass catchers.Ryan O'Leary of Dawg Pound Daily put it plainly: "the writing has been on the wall for Tillman" in Cleveland. His training camp did not do him any favors either. With Concepcion and Boston generating buzz, and Tylan Wallace and Malachi Corley also in the mix, Tillman became one of the easiest roster decisions the Browns had to make.Could Cedric Tillman be a low-cost fix for the Chiefs' receiver room?Kansas City's wide receiver situation heading into the 2026 season is best described as uncertain. Rashee Rice's bounce-back is not guaranteed. Xavier Worthy's health is a question. Tyquan Thornton showed flashes last year but has yet to prove consistency. That is a lot of "what ifs" for a franchise that counts on its passing game to carry playoff runs.Tillman, by contrast, offers something more concrete. He has averaged 11.7 yards per reception in his career, and 40 of his 71 catches moved the chains for a first down. He is big enough to function as a red zone weapon, capable of winning contested catches against single coverage. His ability to work vertically and over the middle could suit Patrick Mahomes, who has seen his receivers struggle to create clean separation in recent seasons.The cost would not be steep. Tillman is in the final year of his rookie deal carrying a cap hit of roughly $3.9 million, according to Spotrac. A late-round pick swap or a simple waiver claim if released outright would be enough to bring him aboard.What does Cedric Tillman's NFL future actually look like?Being cut before Week 1 does not end careers. It redirects them. Tillman is 24, has legitimate size and length, and has shown he can win against NFL-caliber defenders in the right matchups. The question has always been whether Cleveland was the right situation for him to show it.A move to Kansas City, or any offense with a real infrastructure around it, could give Tillman a fair shot to demonstrate what he is actually capable of. Whether Mahomes' system brings out a more dynamic version of him remains to be seen. But at this price point and this stage of the roster cycle, teams searching for receiver help would be making a mistake by not at least exploring the option.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Vince Young story: “Vince had distractions. He enjoyed himself and spent money, and he’d burn it real hard Friday night. So, he’d miss meetings. He’d miss treatment” - From troubled childhood and Texas glory to NFL fallout, bankruptcy, and redemption
articles.summary: NFL News: Vince Young had a troubled childhood. His father left when he was four years old and was in and out of prison. His mother, Felicia, and grandmother, B.
articles.body: Vince Young had a troubled childhood. His father left when he was four years old and was in and out of prison. His mother, Felicia, and grandmother, Bonnie King, raised Young and his two sisters in Houston’s Hiram Clarke neighborhood.According to Sports Illustrated, Felicia worked long hours as a home health aide and also spent much of her time partying. Surrounded by “drinking, partying, drugs, and fighting,” Young’s family struggled with poverty and lived day to day.To escape the chaos around him, Young found a safe place in a tree. He would climb to the top and think about his next goal. Eventually, that goal became football at Madison High School.Young put up unbelievable numbers during his senior year, recording 5,100 total yards and 59 touchdowns. College recruiters sent him letters every day, and his dream was to play for Florida State.Vince Young wanted Florida State but Texas Longhorns chose himYoung wanted Florida State, but there was one problem: the team wanted him to play wide receiver.That terribly broke his heart.Then came the Texas Longhorns.Their head coach at the time, Mack Brown, was doing everything he could to take the team to another level, but the Longhorns had repeatedly failed to get over the hump. Then came Young’s opportunity to change that.Before recruiting him, Brown wanted to learn more about Young’s background, so he visited his home. Young’s grandmother was skeptical.“I don’t know that Texas is gonna play a Black quarterback,” she told Brown.Brown’s response was simple: “I’m gonna play the best quarterback.”Young was thrilled that Texas did not want him to become a wide receiver. The Longhorns wanted him to play quarterback.From then on, there was no stopping him.Vince Young’s legendary National Championship performance against USCYoung eventually led Texas to the national championship game against the two-time reigning champions, the USC Trojans. USC was led by Heisman Trophy winners Matt Leinart and Reggie Bush and entered the game on a 34-game winning streak.But Young delivered one of the greatest performances in college football history.He threw for 267 yards, rushed for another 200 yards, and accounted for three touchdowns. His most memorable moment came on fourth down, when he scored the game-winning touchdown with just 19 seconds remaining.Young was named the game’s MVP and cemented his place in University of Texas history, delivering the Longhorns their first national title since 1970.In the Netflix documentary called “Untold: The Testimony of Vince Young”, Young said he believed he was destined for that moment.“To be that quarterback of that team at that moment, from all the trials and tribulations I’ve been through, was just godly stuff. Godly things. I was meant for that moment. I was meant to be there,” he said.That year, following the national championship, Young entered the NFL Draft.From Texas hero to the Tennessee Titans’ No 3 overall pickThe Tennessee Titans selected Young with the No. 3 overall pick in the first round of the 2006 NFL Draft.However, his arrival in Tennessee was not without controversy.According to the documentary, then-Titans owner Bud Adams drove the decision to draft Young, while head coach Jeff Fisher reportedly opposed the selection.Young had enjoyed a strong coach-quarterback relationship at Texas with Mack Brown. It even led to a national championship title. In the NFL, however, his relationship with Fisher became increasingly fractured.Fisher did not simply disagree with drafting Young; according to Young, the tension became evident throughout his time with the Titans.During Young’s rookie season, Fisher instructed the team plane to leave without him after he arrived late for a flight.“I had just a few rules. The rules were pretty simple,” Fisher explained in the documentary. “So, if you had a problem with that, then you had a problem with me. Vince had distractions. He enjoyed himself and spent money, and he’d burn it real hard Friday night. So, he’d miss meetings. He’d miss treatment.”Despite the troubled relationship, Young had an impressive rookie season. He helped the Titans finish 8-5 in games he started and won the NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year award.The 2008 incident that deepened the riftAnother tumultuous event further damaged the relationship between Young and Fisher.After suffering a knee injury, Young missed a medical examination the following day. He left home with his licensed firearm and without his phone.His concerned mother contacted the Titans and Fisher, who then involved the team therapist and Nashville police amid fears that Young might be suicidal.However, Young later told Sports Illustrated in 2017 that his gun was unloaded and locked in the trunk of his vehicle. He said he was safe and was simply watching football with his friend and teammate, Bo Scaife, while the team was trying to locate him.Young said Fisher called and asked whether he was suicidal. Young said he was fine and simply wanted some space.Fisher asked him to come to the team facility so he could make sure he was okay. However, when Young arrived, he found members of the press waiting there.The incident further damaged the already troubled coach-quarterback relationship.The locker room fallout that ended Vince Young’s Titans careerThe relationship worsened again during the 2010 season.Young tore a tendon in his right thumb during a game, but Fisher refused to let him return to the field. In response, Young threw his shoulder pads and helmet and stormed out of the locker room.“Fisher didn’t let me back into the facilities no more,” Young said in the documentary. “So that’s when I knew I was done in Tennessee.”Young added that it was not how he wanted his career with the Titans to end.“It was definitely not how I wanted to end my career with the Titans, ‘cause they were a team that I really wanted to play with and win a Super Bowl with.”The Titans eventually took matters into their own hands. Fisher was fired in January 2011, and Young was released a few months later in July.Vince Young’s brief NFL stops and early retirementYoung later had brief stints with the Philadelphia Eagles, Green Bay Packers, and Cleveland Browns before officially calling it quits in 2014, at just 31 years old. Today, players are playing beyond 35 and straight into their early 40s, like Aaron Rodgers and Joe Flacco.His NFL career included two Pro Bowl selections, and he finished with a 31-19 record as a starting quarterback.But football was not the only challenge Young faced after his rise to fame in college football.Bankruptcy, lawsuits, and financial recoveryIn 2012, Young filed for bankruptcy.According to FOX Sports, Young sued his former financial adviser, Ronnie T. Peoples, and his former sports agent, Major L. Adams II.Young alleged that they had cheated him out of at least $5.5 million by forging his signatures, falsifying documents, and using a fake email address to secure loans and pay off Adams II’s debts.“I’m over here trying to be the best athlete I can be, believing that I had some guys that I can trust to watch my back and doing what’s in the best interest of me, but they were doing the total opposite,” Young said in the documentary.The case was settled out of court in December 2013. A month later, Young filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy.In a 2017 Sports Illustrated interview, Young said it took him three years to come out of debt and improve his financial situation.Life after footballFast forward to today, and Vince Young has returned to his alma mater.Since 2021, he has worked as a special assistant in the University of Texas athletic department.The former Texas Longhorns star has also built a family of his own. He is married to his high school sweetheart, Candice Young, and they share a son. Young is also the father of two daughters from previous relationships.Vince Young as a father and his efforts to build a different legacyYoung does not want to repeat the mistakes of his own father, who left him when he was four years old. Instead, he wants to be present-present for his children.When his daughter attended her first basketball camp in 2024, Young proudly cheered her on and shared the moment on Instagram.His son, Jordan “Jayman” Young, is a junior at Kinkaid High School in Houston and also plays football. However, Young is determined not to put unnecessary pressure on him.Instead, the former NFL quarterback wants to help build his son’s character and teach him how to be a professional from a young age. His goal is for college coaches to be impressed not only by his son as an athlete, but also by the person he becomes.From a difficult childhood in Houston to one of the greatest performances in college football history, a fractured NFL career, financial struggles, and eventual redemption, Vince Young’s story has been anything but ordinary.He once climbed a tree to escape the chaos around him and dream about his next goal. Years later, after all the trials, tribulations, victories, and setbacks, Young is still focused on what comes next and on building a better legacy for his children.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. But the Dolphins traded him and Jalen Ramsey to the Steelers ahead of the 2025 season for Minkah Fitzpatrick and a late-round pick swap. He didn't replicate his success in Miami with the Steelers, catching just 38 passes for 222 yards and two touchdowns, as quarterback Aaron Rodgers clearly preferred targets like wideout DK Metcalf, tight end Pat Freiermuth and even running back Kenny Gainwell out of the backfield.

Given Smith's disappointing season and the fact that the Steelers saved $7 million against the cap by cutting him, the news didn't come as a major surprise. articles.title: New Christian Gonzalez Contract Rumors Revealed By NFL Insider Ahead of Patriots Season
articles.summary: The New England Patriots' Sept. 9 season opener is fewer than two weeks away, but they reportedly aren't close to agreeing to a new deal with star cornerback Christian Gonzalez.
articles.body:
The New England Patriots' Sept. 9 season opener is fewer than two weeks away, but they reportedly aren't close to agreeing to a new deal with star cornerback Christian Gonzalez.

"I don't think that at any one point here, they've been close to a deal," ESPN's Adam Schefter reported Thursday during an appearance on The Pat McAfee Show while also comparing the situation to Devon Witherspoon and the Seattle Seahawks.

"Witherspoon was going to get done first, and it got done at an average of $33 million per year. The Patriots have not been in that category. But Witherspoon has established a benchmark, and the Patriots haven't gone there. And they weren't there before, and they don't appear to be going there now."

Schefter did suggest things could change in the near future and added, "I think there's probably another push before the season begins or at the start of the season from both sides. … He's too good a player not to try to get something done."

The 2026 campaign is the final one on Gonzalez's contract before a 2027 club option, but he is extension eligible.

Given his standing as one of the best cornerbacks in the league, the Patriots figured to pay him at some point this offseason to make sure he remains with the team for the long-term future. But it has not happened yet, and Gonzalez is growing frustrated with the situation.

"It's frustrating, but I'm focused on the season," he told reporters Tuesday. "I'm focused on here now."

He also didn't exactly fully commit to playing in Week 1:

Gonzalez's comments came after Patriots executive vice president of player personnel Eliot Wolf said during halftime of a preseason game against the Philadelphia Eagles, "Each side is trying to do what's right for them. Christian is a tremendous player that we've been on record multiple times saying we want him to be here, and that hasn't changed. We're going to continue working with his representation to try to get something done."

The cornerback is just 24 years old and coming off a Pro Bowl season that saw him tally 69 tackles and 10 passes defended.

His impact was clear during New England's run to the Super Bowl, as he had an interception in the AFC Championship Game win over the Denver Broncos before posting three passes defended and limiting star receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba to four catches for 27 yards in the Super Bowl loss to the Seahawks.

Considering the Patriots play Seattle again in Week 1, it will surely want Gonzalez on the field and matching up with the reigning Offensive Player of the Year.

First, though, the two sides may need to reach an agreement on his contract.

articles.summary: The final week of NFL preseason games begins Thursday night with four matchups.
articles.body:
The final week of NFL preseason games is upon us.

Each team has one more game to evaluate its personnel before carving out a 53-man regular-season roster and building a practice squad. Some teams approached the preseason with starters playing the first two weeks, intending to sit them this week, while others will have their starters see action only this week.

Thursday's preseason slate consists of four games. The night will begin with the Pittsburgh Steelers taking on the Buffalo Bills . Although a regular-season matchup between these teams would make for a fun quarterback battle, neither Aaron Rodgers nor Josh Allen will suit up.

On Monday, the Cleveland Browns named Deshaun Watson their starting quarterback . But Watson won't play Thursday night against the New England Patriots . His backup, Shedeur Sanders , won't either. That said, Las Vegas Raiders rookie Fernando Mendoza could be in line for more action, this time against the San Francisco 49ers . So far, through two appearances, this year's No. 1 overall pick has completed 18 of 31 passes for 183 yards with a touchdown and an interception.

The night concludes with a SoFi Stadium head-to-head between the Los Angeles Rams and Los Angeles Chargers .

Coaches are being coy about who will play in those games, but we're tracking who's in and who's out:

Notables playing: Some undisclosed Bills starters, QBs Kyle Allen and Shane Buechele (Bills), QBs Will Howard and Drew Allar (Steelers)

Bills fans have seen the last of Allen on the field this preseason. Even though head coach Joe Brady didn't make his full plans for the preseason finale public, he did make a point of telling the media that Allen's preseason was over and that he wouldn't be playing Thursday. Brady, however, also teased that Allen could get the opportunity to call some plays. Buffalo's QB2 competition will take center stage in Highmark Stadium, where Kyle Allen and Shane Buechele will continue to duke it out.

Speaking of reserve signal-callers, mums the word on exactly what kind of playing time Will Howard and Drew Allar will get for the Steelers. After impressing versus the Green Bay Packers in Pittsburgh's opener, they struggled last week against the New York Jets , with Howard notably throwing a pair of first-half interceptions . The Steelers are expected to zero in on Howard and Allar again this week, except it's yet to be seen if Aaron Rodgers will be called upon, too. It sounds as if head coach Mike McCarthy is satisfied with Mason Rudolph 's tape from the opener versus the Packers.

Notables playing: QBs Dillon Gabriel and Taylen Green (Browns)

Notables out: Browns starters, including QB Deshaun Watson; QB Shedeur Sanders (Browns); Patriots starters, including QB Drake Maye and WR A.J. Brown

Browns head coach Todd Monken revealed that he won't be trotting out his starters Thursday against the Patriots . That group includes Watson. He also said Sanders won't be out there. Dillon Gabriel, meanwhile, is in position to play a good portion of the game. Gabriel, whom Cleveland selected in the third round last year and who started six games during the 2025 season, could be fighting for a roster spot if the Browns aren't keen on keeping four QBs. Green, a sixth-round pick from this year's draft, is regarded as a developmental quarterback with tantalizing athleticism ( he wowed at the NFL scouting combine ).

As for New England , it's been prioritizing the health of its first-teamers this preseason. The Patriots aren't deviating from that strategy for the finale. There are still Pats players to watch, though. If the past couple of weeks are any indication, second-year wideout Kyle Williams could get a good bit of run. That's important to monitor after New England traded receiver Kayshon Boutte to the Houston Texans earlier this week .

Notables playing: RGs Jackson Powers-Johnson, Caleb Rogers (Raiders)

Notables out: QB Brock Purdy (49ers), RB Christian McCaffrey (49ers), WR Mike Evans (49ers)

The 49ers are expected to rest many of their starters. San Francisco has been overwhelmed by injuries this summer, so you can't fault head coach Kyle Shanahan for wanting to get his team some rest when he can. Plus, the Niners are gearing up for a short turnaround because of their trip to Australia for their season opener against the Rams .

Shanahan indicated the 49ers will approach this week's game against the Raiders like they did their first preseason game against the Tennessee Titans . So it's likely San Francisco will be without quarterback Brock Purdy, running back Christian McCaffrey and wide receiver Mike Evans, among others. It'll be interesting to keep an eye on rookie wideout De'Zhaun Stribling. The Ole Miss product is intriguing and has piled up 11 preseason receptions. Time will tell if he's given an opportunity to add to that total.

Fernando Mendoza has been racking up reps, even some with the first-team offense, throughout training camp, but Kirk Cousins is still the first-string quarterback … for now . It wouldn't be surprising to see Mendoza receive additional work Thursday in Vegas. Up front, the Raiders are surveying a two-way race for the top spot at right guard. Jackson Powers-Johnson, a 2024 second-round pick, is involved and so is Caleb Rogers, a 2025 third-round pick.

Notables playing: Chargers starters, including QB Justin Herbert and C Jake Slaughter, for "six to nine plays," QB Ty Simpson (Rams), QBs Trey Lance and DJ Uiagalelei (Chargers)

Rams head coach Sean McVay, who famously doesn't play starters in the preseason, wasn't very vocal about his approach to his team's final exhibition game, particularly regarding who would be playing. He did make a point of saying that rookie quarterback Ty Simpson will play. Simpson turned in an eye-catching debut, whereas backup Stetson Bennett IV had the more captivating performance last week .

The Chargers will be rolling out their starters for "six to nine plays" Thursday, according to head coach Jim Harbaugh . As a result, we'll be privy to another glimpse of Justin Herbert operating in the Mike McDaniel offense. Jake Slaughter is expected to be the one snapping him the ball. Slaughter, a rookie out of Florida whom the Chargers took in the second round, is filling the void left by Tyler Biadasz , who was placed on injured reserve last week due to an ACL injury he sustained during a joint practice with the 49ers .

articles.title: Tutu Atwell Reportedly Traded to Rams Ahead of 2026 NFL Season, Dolphins Return Revealed
articles.summary: With Sunday's NFL deadline to cut rosters to 53 players looming, the Miami Dolphins and Los Angeles Rams reportedly made a trade involving two offensive skill players.
articles.body:
With Sunday's NFL deadline to cut rosters to 53 players looming, the Miami Dolphins and Los Angeles Rams reportedly made a trade involving two offensive skill players.

ESPN's Adam Schefter reported Thursday the Dolphins traded wide receiver Tutu Atwell to the Rams in exchange for running back Jarquez Hunter.

Both players likely would have struggled for consistent opportunities on their previous teams.

Hunter was behind Kyren Williams and Blake Corum in Los Angeles and may have lost carries to Ronnie Rivers as well. Atwell would have been competing with Jalen Tolbert, Malik Washington and Caleb Douglas, among others in Miami.

While Atwell still isn't going to see a ton of targets in Los Angeles with Puka Nacua and Davante Adams making up one of the best one-two receiver punches in the league, he is at least going back to a familiar location.

He played for the Rams from 2021 through 2025 and isn't far removed from the 2024 season when he finished with 42 catches for 562 yards. There is a chemistry in place with quarterback Matthew Stafford even if he was largely an afterthought in the offense last season on the way to 192 receiving yards.

Ideally for the Rams, Atwell can work in the slot and take advantage of favorable matchups when opposing defenses are too focused on Nacua and Adams. If he does that, he could be something of a familiar safety valve for Stafford as the NFC West team attempts to make another deep playoff run.

As for Hunter, he didn't see a single carry for the Rams last season.

Perhaps this change of scenery will lead to more opportunities for the 2025 fourth-round pick when the Dolphins mix in other backs outside of De'Von Achane.

articles.title: New Fantasy Football 2026 Mock Draft Strategy and Cheat Sheet for Opening Rounds
articles.summary: The NFL preseason is nearing its conclusion, which means that fantasy managers will soon transition from mock drafts to the real thing. However, there's still time to cram in a few mock drafts to help put the finishing touches on preseason preparation.
articles.body:
The NFL preseason is nearing its conclusion, which means that fantasy managers will soon transition from mock drafts to the real thing. However, there's still time to cram in a few mock drafts to help put the finishing touches on preseason preparation.

Of course, getting the most out of mock drafts requires more than making a few practice picks. Smart managers use a variety of tried-and-true strategies to glean the most useful information.

Here, you find a look at some of the top strategies for mocking the early rounds, along with a cheat sheet for the key early-round targets and the results of a mock draft conducted with FantasyPros' Mock Draft Simulator .

Make a Big Board Beforehand and Don't Stop With One Mock

This one might seem obvious. However, some managers really will run a single mock, be happy with the results, and deem themselves ready for their actual draft. The problem is that no two drafts are ever the same, and the odds of perfectly mirroring that lone mock are practically zero.

By running multiple mocks, managers can try out different strategies, which they should. This should provide an idea of the best ways to land the most value on a personalized big board. Does doubling up on RBs early leave you lacking at WR while going WR first consistently yields a more balanced roster? That's valuable information to have heading into a live draft.

And, yes, you should look to set your own draft board before digging into mock drafts. Fantasy rankings are great, but you're going to feel much better about your team when you land players you personally believe in.

Working through multiple mocks can also help you plot out a pivot plan, which every manager should have. Anyone who plays fantasy long enough will eventually run into that draft where a rogue manager reaches heavily at a position and sparks a very unexpected run.

In such a scenario, the best managers pivot instead of making panic picks.

If you decide your goal in the early rounds is to start with some combination of two RBs and a WR, it's good to have a backup plan for if/when that strategy is no longer viable. Try a zero-RB approach or an RB-TE-WR strategy to see which Plan B best meshes with your preferred results.

We're certainly not saying that you have to treat mock drafts like it's AP psychology. However, it's good to have a notepad handy when running through mocks.

For one thing, it's wise to keep tabs on how different strategies are stacking up. It's also a good idea to note any draft trends you start to notice during your mock-drafting journey.

Have you noticed that favorite sleeper slowly rising up the draft order? Tracking his draft range can help you avoid missing out in your live draft.

Jaxon Smith-Njigba, WR, Seattle Seahawks

Christian McCaffrey, RB, San Francisco 49ers

Omarion Hampton, RB, Los Angeles Chargers

Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase is trending as the top overall pick in many fantasy formats. He's certainly worthy of the hype, but this also means that managers picking as late as fourth have a realistic chance of grabbing Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs or Atlanta Falcons running back Bijan Robinson.

Given the scarcity of true high-volume backs in 2026, managers should feel very good about kicking off a draft with either Robinson or Gibbs—who finished second and third, respectively, among RBs in point-per-reception (PPR) leagues.

Middle 4: Puka Nacua or Jaxon Smith-Njigba

Last season, Los Angeles Rams wideout Puka Nacua and Seattle Seahawks receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba finished first and second, respectively, among WRs in PPR leagues. They're trending below Chase this preseason because Joe Burrow is healthy. However, both receivers could again finish in the top two.

Nacua and Smith-Njigba are excellent players to target in the middle of Round 1, should either be pushed out of the top five.

Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Justin Jefferson is trending as a late-first-round pick, which leaves managers with a prime opportunity to buy low.

Yes, Jefferson had a down year as Minnesota's offense stumbled through the 2025 season. However, he finished the previous season as WR2 and should be poised for a bounce-back campaign with Kyler Murray taking over at quarterback for the Vikings.

Christian McCaffrey, San Francisco 49ers

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham gets cheeky and celebrates Dolly Parton, Dolphins fans brace for Tua & Dunkin's disrespect!
articles.summary: Sophie Cunningham's cheeky Dolly Parton tribute, Dunkin's early pumpkin coffee launch, and the debate over booing Tua in his Falcons return.
articles.body: 'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday–Friday on OutKick.com. Over the hump and safely into the second half of the week. We're 48 hours away from college football, boys and girls. Two sleeps. That's it. Will it feel like a college football Saturday? A real one? Eh. Probably not. No GameDay. No Big Noon. No full slate. But after the insufferable summer we've just endured, a little UNC-TCU in Dublin will be welcomed with open arms. Everyone is out to get Bill Belichick right now. Paul Finebaum has been slandering the GOAT for months over on ESPN. It's disgusting. ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW! Please, Lord, let UNC win. I need it. Let's roll. Welcome to a Thursday Nightcaps — the one where the Dolly Parton tributes keep rolling in, both from you guys AND from Sophie Cunningham. I've been scanning the other WNBA socials and didn't see anyone else pay their respects to Dolly. Stunning! What else? I've got an embarrassing Wednesday afternoon crowd out west, a loaded inbox after yesterday's question (I knew it would be), Dolphins fans are currently arguing about the dumbest thing imaginable, and you'll never guess what's already back at my local Dunks. Disgusting. You'll see. Grab you a regular coffee because it's only August 27th and you have an ounce of self-respect, and settle in for a Thursday 'Cap! Sophie Cunningham gets cheeky and respects Dolly Parton Couple things ... SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM THROWS ON A BACKLESS TOP AND OVERTAKES CAITLIN CLARK, TRUMP WAVES THE FLAG & GRUDEN'S BACK! We all caught up now? Good! Now, let's get this class started with Sophie Cunningham respecting Dolly Parton with a social media post that included the caption: "My weaknesses have always been food and men — in that order." Dolly Parton Worst sports moments! Wild little ride there from Sophie. What a twist at the end, too! Didn't see it coming. Not sure what was going on there or who Sophie was mooning, but we're all here to have fun, right? Lord knows I'd take that over the nonsense that happened in Chicago earlier this week. OK, let's keep the line moving and check the mailbox before we run out of time. Yesterday, I asked everyone for their top five heartbreaking moments as a sports fan. As expected, you all brought it. From Kevin W: 1. Red sox come back from 3. 2. Wide right 3. Music city miracle…it was a forward pass 4. 13 seconds 5. It was a catch not an interception. - I take it Kevin is a Bills and Yankees fan. Just a hunch. From Matt C: 1. As a Devils fan, Matteau in 2OT in '94. It just cannot possibly get any worse than that in sports, although Bills fans could have an argument. 2. But as a Knicks fan, Charles Smith's missed layups against the Bulls in '93. That was our year. 3. As a Mets fan, Yadier Molina's homer in the top of the 9th, 2006 NLCS Game 7. It took me weeks to recover. 4. Back to the Knicks, Starks shooting 2-18 in the '94 Finals Game 7 against the Rockets. That was our year. 5. I'll just leave this slot reserved for Michael Jordan. It's an amalgamation of bad memories at this point. And in each of them, it was definitely our year. I still say the 90s Knicks have an argument as a legitimate dynasty, despite no ring. - The 2006 NLCS was incredible. One of my favorite postseason baseball series ever. From Brian S: 1. 1987 playoffs, finally ready to vanquish the Celtics. Isiah Thomas inbound pass stolen by Larry Bird, fed to Dennis Johnson, accompanied by that Johnny Most radio call. 2. 1987 was a great year! Syracuse missing countless FTs down the stretch, then having Keith Smart ripping the heart out of its first chance at a natty with the only shot he’ll ever be remembered for. 3. Carlos Beltran, bat on shoulder, watching Adam Wainwright’s curve end the 2006 NLCS. 4. Here’s a double-dipper San Francisco treat: Lions gagging on a 24-7 halftime lead to 49ers in 2025 NFC title game; Giants somehow blow a 38-14 third quarter lead to 49ers in the 2002 Wild Card. 5. And, most recently, the Mets trading Pete Crow Armstrong for Javy "Thumbs Down" Baez. That one might ascend higher as the years continue. - I'm sensing a theme with New York sports fans today. You guys have had it ROUGH! Angels in the outfield & booing a former player? That picture of Trump watching Beltran strikeout to end the series resurfaces every few years, and it mesmerizes me every time. What a game. What a series. Who knew we'd work in so much Mets-Cards '06 NLCS talk into today's class? It's why we win (hypothetical) awards! OK, let's rapid-fire this Thursday class into a big night of FCS football. That's right. FCS football: Forget Saturday ... we get 22 (!!!) FCS football games tonight. Seems excessive, but I'll take anything after this summer. Not sure why ESPN couldn't be bothered to put one on an actual network, but I reckon they have to sell those stupid ESPN+ subscriptions somehow. Here's the real question, though: Do we think those 22 FCS games will have more butts in the seats than yesterday's Indians-Angels game did? Lordy. What a scene! The official box score says they had over 25,000 fans in attendance. Do you buy that? Come on. I don't blame Angels fans for one second, by the way. In a historically down year for the American League, they are still, somehow, the worst team in baseball. Do you understand how hard it is for an AL team to be out of the playoff race right now? And yes, I know it was ... hot ... in Anaheim yesterday. The weather man tells me it was 92 degrees. The sun was out. A lot of the fans moved to shadier pastures in the stadium. I get it. But still, it's such a bad look for a professional baseball team. Yikes. On the way out, I'd like to leave everyone here with another question: Do players who left a team deserve to get booed upon their return? Dolphins fans are planning to boo the heck out of Tua when he comes back tomorrow night as the preseason starter for the Falcons ... And they absolutely, unequivocally should. I was a HUGE Tua guy for years. Massive. But then he signed a lucrative deal that he didn't deserve, became insufferably cocky and unlikeable, and started playing like dog-you-know-what before getting cut. He also hamstrung the franchise with all of his dead money, although that goes on the GM as much as it does Tua. But the broader point? Yes, former players who left on bad terms should get booed when they return. Could you imagine Philly fans having this debate? Those sickos boo their teams three minutes into a new season! I've seen it. And I love it. Anyway, let me know! See you tomorrow. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Booing Tua OK? Email me at Zach.Dean@OutKick.com.

articles.title: Louisiana governor balks at SEC's ban on former NFL players
articles.summary: Two distinct schools of thought have emerged regarding the recent manifestation of the chaos in college football.
articles.body:
Two distinct schools of thought have emerged regarding the recent manifestation of the chaos in college football. One relies on using the unprecedented ability of former NFL players to return to college for another season as fuel to turn the Protect College Sports Act into the law of the land. The other arises from a burning desire to win as many football games as possible right now.

It has created a scenario in which conferences like the SEC, the Big Ten, and most recently the Big 12 have adopted performative rules aimed at building political momentum for antitrust exemption and schools like LSU have jumped on the opportunity to enhance the roster with the addition of players who had been under contract with NFL teams.

Not surprisingly, Louisiana Governor Jeff Landry is siding with his state's flagship football program.

"This whole thing is ridiculous. Don't hate the player, hate the game ," Landry said regarding the SEC's rule, via John Blau of the Advocate .

"I've been saying for a year that college sports need to be fixed," Landry added. "The NCAA could have done it. Congress could have done it. Neither did. Now the SEC is creating a legal mess over athletes it told were out of eligibility, only to change the rules afterward."

The legal mess keeps getting messier. The conferences potentially are violating the court order allowing players to get the fifth year that the NCAA has now baked into the rules.

"The SEC accepted the courts' decisions on Diego Pavia and Trinidad Chambliss ," Landry said. "Why is this different? You can't tell athletes their college careers are over, watch them move on, change the rules later, and then punish them for not predicting the future."

Of course, Landry is only taking that position because LSU wants to add these players. If LSU coach Lane Kiffin was content to move forward with the players he has and if, say, Georgia wanted to sign former NFL players who have secured a fifth year through the courts, Landry would be aggressively waving an SEC flag and complaining about Georgia's effort to violate the spirit of amateur athletics.

Everyone involved in this fiasco is acting in their own interests. And the ultimate prize continues to be creating enough of a mess that Congress will pass the Protect College Sports Act under the guise of injecting normalcy into the process — while also stripping the players of their earning potential and mobility.

You know, the two things that got Kiffin to ditch Ole Miss during the 2025 season and pounce on the chance to work for LSU.

articles.title: Seahawks’ Jaxon Smith-Njigba Headlines Massive $483 Million Offseason Spending Spree
articles.summary: Following a breakout season in which he solidified himself as the best receiver in football, Jaxon Smith-Njigba helped lead the Seattle Seahawks to a Super B...
articles.body:
Following a breakout season in which he solidified himself as the best receiver in football, Jaxon Smith-Njigba helped lead the Seattle Seahawks to a Super Bowl LX victory over the New England Patriots . The front office rewarded his impressive performance by signing him to a massive four-year, $168.6 million contract extension, officially making him the highest-paid wide receiver in NFL history.

However, the 2023 first-round pick isn't the only building block who secured a major payday this offseason. According to recent front-office reports, the Seahawks have committed roughly $483.6 million to keeping their championship core together, with Smith-Njigba's record-breaking deal serving as the crown jewel.

Seattle extends Jaxon Smith-Njigba and locks up championship core

Smith-Njigba was unstoppable in 2025, leading the NFL with 1,793 receiving yards and 119 receptions. Those solid numbers earned him First-Team All-Pro honors and the AP Offensive Player of the Year award.

Seattle didn't waste any time locking him down, giving the 24-year-old a four-year extension with $120 million guaranteed. His $42.15 million average annual salary surpassed Ja'Marr Chase's as the highest-paid wide receiver contract in NFL history, keeping him in Seattle through 2031.

"This year has been great," Smith-Njigba said during Seahawks minicamp . "It's brought me a lot of great things, and things to learn and overcome and trophies and parades and stuff like that."

His record-breaking contract set the tone for a massive offseason spending spree. Seattle's defense led the NFL in fewest points allowed last year, and the Seahawks didn't shy away from spending millions more to keep that entire championship group together.

Cornerback Devon Witherspoon followed suit with a massive four-year, $132 million extension. The deal includes $101 million guaranteed and pays him $33 million per year, surpassing the Cleveland Browns ' Denzel Ward to make him the highest-paid cornerback in NFL history. The three-time Pro Bowler had a dominant performance in the Super Bowl, including a big sack and a vicious hit on the Patriots' signal-caller Drake Maye that set up a game-sealing defensive touchdown.

"It feels good. Long time coming," Witherspoon said after signing . "We just had to get it done. I'm thankful."

The front office also locked down its defensive line by signing star pass rusher Leonard Williams to a three-year, $90 million deal and extending young edge threat Derick Hall for three years and $42 million.

In addition, they re-signed Rashid Shaheed to a three-year, $51 million contract, with experts expecting him to have a breakout 2026 season . With these five deals, general manager John Schneider showed that his strategy is to pay the core players and keep the championship roster together to chase another title.
